For users who prefer direct market participation, RIFT also offers Manual Trading and Futures Trading functionality. This gives traders the flexibility to execute their own strategies, manage positions, and take advantage of market opportunities in real time.

videos.summary_source_text:
Hindi - 08.09.26 - RIFT Education Day RIFT is a modern trading platform that combines automated trading, manual trading, futures trading, and educational tools into one ecosystem.

Designed for both beginners and experienced traders, RIFT aims to simplify access to financial markets while providing users with tools that can help them participate more efficiently.

One of the key features of RIFT is its Auto Trading Engine, which allows users to allocate capital into automated trading strategies designed to operate without the need for constant monitoring. This enables participants to remain active in the markets without spending hours each day analyzing charts or placing trades manually.

For users who prefer direct market participation, RIFT also offers Manual Trading and Futures Trading functionality. This gives traders the flexibility to execute their own strategies, manage positions, and take advantage of market opportunities in real time.

RIFT is built around a non-custodial philosophy, meaning users maintain control of their own funds rather than depositing them into a centralized company account. This approach aligns with the growing demand for greater transparency, security, and user control within the digital asset industry.

Beyond trading, RIFT focuses heavily on education. Through training sessions, community support, and ongoing learning resources, users can develop a deeper understanding of trading, risk management, market psychology, and financial technology.

The platform also incorporates modern technologies such as AI-driven infrastructure, advanced execution systems, copy trading capabilities, and future integrations designed to create a more connected and intelligent trading environment.

Whether you are completely new to trading, looking for automated solutions, interested in futures markets, or seeking to expand your financial knowledge, RIFT aims to provide a complete ecosystem where users can learn, participate, and grow.

One of the strongest measurements of overall fitness and longevity is VO2 max, which reflects how efficiently your body uses oxygen to produce energy in the mitochondria.

🌟 Take the 2-minute Health Lever Quiz: https://drbrg.co/4g9ZXO6

Just so you know, my full line of high-quality supplements is available on Amazon — search Dr. Berg Supplements. 

To improve VO2 max and support healthy aging:
• Walk for 30 to 60 minutes a few times each week
• Try Norwegian 4x4 interval training
• Build muscle with resistance training
• Use intermittent fasting to support autophagy and mitochondrial health

Low VO2 max is strongly associated with poor health outcomes, which is why improving cardiovascular fitness and maintaining muscle become even more important as you age.

videos.summary_source_text:
The Worst Drink for Your Liver The worst drink for your liver may be hard liquor. Unlike beer or wine, concentrated alcohol delivers a large amount of ethanol quickly, forcing the liver to process more of the toxic byproduct acetaldehyde.

🌟 Take the 2-minute Health Lever Quiz: https://drbrg.co/46fqWDx

Just so you know, my full line of high-quality supplements is available on Amazon — search Dr. Berg Supplements. 

Acetaldehyde can:
• Damage liver cells
• Increase inflammation
• Interfere with the liver’s ability to regenerate
• Increase the risk of fatty liver and other liver problems

Even a couple of shots per day can place significant stress on the liver over time.

videos.summary_source_text:
How Elite Players Hit Perfect One-Timers The Downhill Skating System is the mechanics-first approach that unlocks effortless, controlled speed on the ice without extra conditioning, pushing or “trying harder.” Inspired by the movement signatures of players like Connor McDavid, Nathan MacKinnon, Cale Makar, Quinn Hughes, and other elite NHL skaters, this system teaches you how to move on the ice with gravity, using your body's own stretch shortening cycles mixed with the most efficient footwork patterns and various skating mechanics.

Most players skate “uphill”: stiff, blocky, pushing hard, creating tension and burning energy like we were always taught in traditional powerskating. Downhill skating flips that model. By using counter rotation, proper joint angles, and natural gravitational momentum, we teach you move faster with less effort.

Inside the Downhill Skating System, players learn to:

1) Unlock the inner spring for better acceleration.
2)Use different footwork patterns to add options, deception and effortlessness. 
3)Proper joint alignment for efficiency and balance instead of creating tension with push strides.

Apply NHL-base mechanics like shin angle, Y-angle, rhythm and cadence. Generate speed using the rocker, with heel pressure and subtle weight transfers.

This system is not what players would learn in traditional, outdated power skating methods. It’s a biomechanics-based operating system designed to match your body type and natural movement patterns.

Whether you’re trying to improve the forward stride, lateral movements, deception, or posture, Downhill Skating reveals the hidden mechanics the NHL’s best rely on, and shows you how to plug them into your game step by step.

If you’re ready to skate faster with less effort, flow through transitions, and move with the smoothness of the world’s best players, the Downhill Skating System is your blueprint to faster player development.

videos.title: Don’t Put That Toothbrush Back in Your Mouth Until You See This | Dr. Mandell
videos.summary_source_text:
Don’t Put That Toothbrush Back in Your Mouth Until You See This | Dr. Mandell Your toothbrush goes into your mouth every morning and every night, but most people never stop to think about what may be sitting between those bristles before they use it again. In this video, I explain how saliva, plaque, food particles, moisture, bathroom surfaces, dirty toothbrush holders, touching bristles with your hands, and poor storage habits can all contribute to contamination over time. You’ll learn why allowing your toothbrush to stay wet can matter, why covering it while it is still damp may not be the best idea, how toilet aerosols can spread through the bathroom environment, why toothbrush heads should not touch each other, and why sharing a toothbrush is never a good idea. I’ll also explain what researchers have found on used toothbrushes, including different bacteria and microorganisms under certain conditions, while making it clear that finding germs does not automatically mean your toothbrush is going to make you sick. The real goal is simple: reduce unnecessary contamination, allow the brush to dry properly, store it intelligently, clean the holder regularly, and replace the toothbrush or electric brush head when the bristles become worn or about every three to four months. These are small habits, but when you think about how many hundreds of times that toothbrush goes directly into your mouth every year, they are worth paying attention to. Better health often starts with noticing the little things you do every single day.

The real goal is simple: reduce unnecessary contamination, allow the brush to dry properly, store it intelligently, clean the holder regularly, and replace the toothbrush or electric brush head when the bristles become worn or about every three to four months. These are small habits, but when you think about how many hundreds of times that toothbrush goes directly into your mouth every year, they are worth paying attention to. Better health often starts with noticing the little things you do every single day.

videos.title: Gemini 4: 10M Context Window & The Race to AGI
videos.summary_source_text:
Gemini 4: 10M Context Window & The Race to AGI Link to our newsletter: https://bitbiased.ai/

Sundar Pichai just confirmed that Google is training Gemini 4 — and the most important part may be what he admitted immediately around that announcement.

On Alphabet’s Q2 2026 earnings call, Pichai said the next generation of frontier AI will require “much larger base models,” confirmed Gemini 4 is already being trained, and described Google as being “very ambitious” with it. But despite the speculation already building around Gemini 4, Google has revealed almost nothing else: no parameter count, no benchmark scores, no model card, and no release date.

That gap between what Google has actually confirmed and what the internet is already claiming is where this story gets interesting.

Gemini’s history gives us some clues. Gemini 1.5 brought a Mixture-of-Experts architecture and a million-token context window. Gemini 2.0 pushed into native multimodal output and agentic tool use. Later generations expanded Google’s focus on extended reasoning through Deep Think. If Google continues that pattern, Gemini 4 probably won’t just be about making the model larger — it will need a meaningful capability leap.

Google has acknowledged that coding and agentic coding remain areas where it needs to improve. That makes reliable multi-step agents and coding performance particularly important as Gemini 4 moves toward the frontier.

The baseline it has to beat is already formidable. Gemini 3.8 Flash, released September 2, 2026, is described by Google as its best reasoning and coding model yet at the same speed and low cost as 3.7. Google reports a 54.9% score on Humanity’s Last Exam, Verified, while pricing remains $0.75 per million input tokens and $3.75 per million output tokens through the end of 2026.

Google has also introduced Gemini 3.8 Flash Cyber, a restricted defensive cybersecurity model designed to find and patch software vulnerabilities for vetted government agencies and infrastructure operators through the Fairwind Program.

Then there’s the hardware behind all of this.

Google’s Ironwood TPUs deliver 4,614 teraflops of FP8 compute per chip with 192GB of high-bandwidth memory. Connect nearly 10,000 of them into a TPU superpod and Google says the system reaches 42.5 exaflops of FP8 compute. Anthropic has also secured access to as many as one million Google TPUs, showing just how enormous Google’s AI infrastructure operation has become.

And Google is spending accordingly. Alphabet has poured enormous amounts of capital into AI infrastructure and compute, while Google is even pursuing advanced nuclear power through its partnership with Kairos Power. The planned capacity reaches up to 500 megawatts by 2035, including the Hermes 2 project intended to support electricity demand associated with Google’s data centers.

But none of that tells us exactly what Gemini 4 will be.

The strongest clue remains Pichai’s emphasis on larger base models combined with Google’s admitted weakness in agentic coding. A Gemini 4 focused on stronger coding, longer autonomous workflows, and more reliable multi-step agents would fit Google’s trajectory — but until Google confirms those capabilities, that remains extrapolation rather than fact.

And the competition won’t wait.

Claude remains a major force in enterprise coding, while OpenAI continues pushing its own frontier models. Google’s potential advantage may not simply be benchmark leadership, but economics. Gemini 3.8 Flash’s token pricing dramatically undercuts the current frontier pricing cited for OpenAI and Anthropic in this analysis. If Google can preserve anything close to that cost advantage while making Gemini 4 substantially more capable, the real competition may become less about which model wins a benchmark and more about intelligence per dollar.

There’s also a much bigger question. Google DeepMind CEO Demis Hassabis has discussed AGI arriving around 2030, give or take, while also pointing to major unsolved problems including continual learning, persistent memory, and grounded understanding of the physical world. Simply making a base model larger does not automatically solve those problems.

So the most revealing Gemini 4 story right now isn’t a leaked parameter count or a supposed benchmark.

It’s that Google has publicly acknowledged the frontier is moving fast enough that its current models aren’t enough — and it is committing enormous models, custom TPUs, infrastructure spending, and power capacity to what comes next.

CHAPTERS

00:53 The One Confirmed Sentence, And Why It Matters
01:56 How Google Actually Got Here
03:54 What Gemini 4 Actually Has To Beat
06:03 The Hardware Google Is Betting Everything On
07:27 Google Is Spending Like This Is The Whole Company
08:50 So What Might Gemini 4 Actually Be?
10:08 The Competition Isn't Standing Still Either
11:46 When, And What It Actually Means
13:18 The Verdict

Claude remains a major force in enterprise coding, while OpenAI continues pushing its own frontier models. Google’s potential advantage may not simply be benchmark leadership, but economics. Gemini 3.8 Flash’s token pricing dramatically undercuts the current frontier pricing cited for OpenAI and Anthropic in this analysis. If Google can preserve anything close to that cost advantage while making Gemini 4 substantially more capable, the real competition may become less about which model wins a benchmark and more about intelligence per dollar.

There’s also a much bigger question. Google DeepMind CEO Demis Hassabis has discussed AGI arriving around 2030, give or take, while also pointing to major unsolved problems including continual learning, persistent memory, and grounded understanding of the physical world. Simply making a base model larger does not automatically solve those problems.

So the most revealing Gemini 4 story right now isn’t a leaked parameter count or a supposed benchmark.

It’s that Google has publicly acknowledged the frontier is moving fast enough that its current models aren’t enough — and it is committing enormous models, custom TPUs, infrastructure spending, and power capacity to what comes next.

videos.title: People are Creating INSANE Things With GPT-6 (Astra)
videos.summary_source_text:
People are Creating INSANE Things With GPT-6 (Astra) Link to our newsletter: https://bitbiased.ai/

OpenAI’s GPT-6 Astra scored 95.9% geometry overlap on BenchCAD, versus 83.3% for GPT-5.6 Sol and 84.3% for Claude Fable 5.1.5. But that benchmark isn’t the most interesting part of the launch.

The bigger story is what Astra can reportedly do inside real software: open Blender and build an editable furnished house, route a circuit board in KiCad, create playable games, operate business software, and reconstruct 3D geometry from limited visual input.

These aren’t just AI-generated images. The strongest Astra demos produce editable files, playable environments, and working projects that humans can open and continue working on.

But that’s also where the story gets complicated.

GPT-6 Astra launched under the model ID gpt-6-astra at $10 per million input tokens and $50 per million output tokens through the API. According to OpenAI, it scores 57.9% on Terminal-Bench 4.0 and 72.6% on OSWorld, a benchmark designed to test whether an agent can operate real desktop interfaces.

That OSWorld result helps explain almost everything else. Astra isn’t simply answering questions about professional software. It’s increasingly capable of driving the software itself.

One of the clearest examples is Solace House, a Blender project published by OpenAI developer Thomas Ricouard. Astra generated architecture, furniture, materials, and lighting from a text brief before the project was exported into Unreal Engine 5 as a walkable environment. Crucially, this was an actual .blend project rather than just a rendered image.

But Astra didn’t create everything from nothing. The project combined original modeling and procedural construction with existing Poly Haven assets and textures, while Ricouard guided the process through multiple prompts.

The same distinction matters with Astra’s game demos.

Developer Pietro Schirano showed Tidal Rush, a playable tropical kart racer reportedly generated from a single prompt. Other demonstrations include underwater exploration, a PS1-style Beyblade arena, and a jet-ski racer. But unlike Tidal Rush, several of those projects currently exist publicly as posts and clips rather than downloadable builds or code.

Inside an actual game studio, Playco says Astra turned one gray-box prototype into three themed playable variants in a single run. According to an OpenAI customer case study, all three worked on the first attempt and required 50% fewer manual fixes than comparable GPT-5.6 workflows. That’s useful production evidence, but it’s still a vendor case study rather than an independent test.

Then there are browser games including Hollowflux, Velocity Loop, Sunwake, and Void Explorer. These matter because they can actually be played rather than simply watched in a launch reel.

Astra’s capabilities also extend beyond creative software. One demo shows a custom micro-console keypad reconstructed as detailed 3D geometry from a photo. Another shows Astra taking an electronic schematic and routing a PCB inside KiCad in roughly two minutes and fifty-four seconds.

The PCB example comes with an important limitation. Routing a board doesn’t necessarily prove that a model understands all of the manufacturing and engineering constraints involved in complex, high-speed, or dense PCB designs. Outside engineers have questioned how far these demonstrations can be generalized beyond relatively simple boards.

Astra has also been demonstrated operating browser-based CRM software, working inside the Flora design environment, and reverse-engineering a closed Bluetooth protocol for a Divoom LED speaker.

So how much of this is actually Astra?

That’s what we investigate: which demos can be independently tested, which rely on vendor claims or social posts, how much human guidance is still involved, and how heavily Astra depends on existing engines, assets, libraries, and professional software.

The real advance may be narrower than “AI can build everything from scratch” — but potentially much more practical.

Astra is showing what happens when an AI model stops merely telling you how to use professional software and starts operating that software itself, handing back editable work instead of a picture of what the finished result might look like.

CHAPTERS

02:02 What OpenAI Actually Shipped
04:34 The House That Wasn't Rendered, It Was Built
06:26 AI Making Games You Can Actually Play
07:47 Inside an Actual Game Studio
08:49 Browser Games Anyone Can Click Into Right Now
09:27 From a Photo to a 3D Model, From a Schematic to a Working Board
11:25 Beyond Creative Tools: Running Business Software By Itself
12:46 How Much of This Is Actually Astra

videos.summary_source_text:
Judy Murray: The Disruptor Who Raised World Champions | On The Road W/ Iona Stephen Judy Murray sits down with Iona Stephen for a fascinating conversation about family, tennis, opportunity and the importance of giving young players the chance to succeed.

Judy reflects on growing up playing tennis in Scotland, raising Andy and Jamie Murray, and the lengths she went to give her sons the best possible opportunities in the sport. She also shares her passion for improving funding and access for junior and girls’ tennis in Scotland, and why she continues to push for change.

There’s a brilliant story about Judy’s conversation with tennis legend Billie Jean King, who recognised something familiar in Judy, telling her that she was a “disruptor”, just like her.

And away from tennis, Judy talks about her newfound love of golf and what has drawn her to the game, as well as her appearance on Strictly Come Dancing.

A candid and inspiring conversation with one of the most influential figures in British tennis.

videos.summary_source_text:
I Let GPT-6 Astra Edit In DaVinci Resolve 21.1 I handed GPT-6 Astra my raw 75 minute recording and let it edit the whole thing inside DaVinci Resolve 21.1, through the new MCP server Blackmagic just shipped. Not computer use, not a cursor clicking around the screen. I did not touch the timeline.

It ran the transcription, put the program and the screen share on separate video tracks, cut 75 minutes down to 22 across 96 edits, picked 10 screen share cutaways on its own, built a lower third, graded the footage, checked the loudness against YouTube's target and rendered the finished 4K file.

The 25 Best Carolina Hurricanes Players of All-Time Part 7 Over the last six parts of the series, we've dived into the Top 25 Carolina Hurricanes players of All-Time, counting down from 25 to 9. In Part 7, we cover spots 8 to 6. Who made it just outside of the top five? On the Tuesday Edition of Locked On Hurricanes, Zach begins the show by sharing his thoughts on Justin Williams being the 8th-best Hurricanes player of all-time. In 449 games, Williams had 316 points through eight seasons with the Hurricanes. While he did come back after playing for a time with the Los Angeles Kings and the Washington Capitals, he was a big part of the new era of Hurricanes hockey with Rod Brind'Amour as the head coach. How huge was his impact with the team during his time in Raleigh? Secondly, Zach shares his thoughts on why Jordan Staal is the 7th-best player for the Hurricanes all-time. In 972 games, he has 499 points, a Conn Smythe, and a Stanley Cup. The current captain of the team just helped the team win their second-ever Stanley Cup, especially after scoring five goals in six games in the Cup Final. While he just missed out on the top five, how huge has Staal been since joining the team in 2012-13? Finally, Zach concludes the show by sharing his thoughts on Ron Francis being the 6th-best player in Hurricanes history. While this take could be controversial, Francis, despite leading the franchise in goals and points, scored most of those as a Hartford Whaler. In terms of relocation, is Francis the best of all-time? videos.summary_source_text:
How home hero Kimi made history at Monza | Italian GP Review | F1 Nation Podcast Tom Clarkson is joined by Lawrence Barretto and Davide Valsecchi to analyse an extraordinary Italian Grand Prix, which saw Kimi Antonelli climb from 19th on the grid to become the first Italian Formula 1 driver to win their home race in 60 years.

How did Antonelli complete such an incredible comeback? Where does his victory rank among the greatest drives in F1 history? And what will be going through George Russell’s head after failing to capitalise on Kimi’s grid penalty?

Lewis Hamilton has suggested that Ferrari need to introduce rules of engagement after he felt Ferrari teammate Charles Leclerc pushed him off into the gravel at Turn 2 on the opening lap. The guys share their thoughts on that incident, what they think caused Leclerc’s race-ending crash on the following lap and how Team Principal Fred Vasseur needs to address the situation between his drivers.

Also on the agenda: how did Max Verstappen secure his fifth podium of the season? Did McLaren exceed expectations in Monza? And what does Pierre Gasly’s remarkable pole position tell us about Alpine’s progress?

videos.title: 481. Tips för att anlita hantverkare och renovera (ekonomiskt) rätt | Christopher Bolin, ComfyLiving
videos.summary_source_text:
481. Tips för att anlita hantverkare och renovera (ekonomiskt) rätt | Christopher Bolin, ComfyLiving Vad är en rimlig timtaxa för en hantverkare? Ska man välja rörligt eller fast pris? Hur får man tag i rätt hantverkare? Vad kan man, bör man och vad ska man absolute inte renovera själv? Hur ska man tänka kring materialpåslag? Vad kan vi som har tummen mitt i handen - eller prioriterar energi och annat - göra? 

Det är några av sakerna vi diskuterar i dagens avsnittet med Christopher Bolin, communitymedlem och VD på Comfy Living som vi anlitat flera gånger under året för att få hantverkshjälp och slippa klassiskt strul.

För tydlighetens skull: Detta avsnitt är ett samarbete med och reklam för Comfy Living som vi använt under året för att få hjälp hemma med allt från fönsterbyte, byte av pax-fläkt, lagning av sprucken platta i badrummet och massa annat. För dessa tjänster har vi betalat samma pris som alla andra. 

I avsnittet kommer vi in på några av hans erfarenheter men han ger även en hel del tips på vad man kan tänka på när man renoverar själv eller anlitar hantverkare: 

▸ En bra tumregel är att räkna ca 1 000 kronor i timmen inklusive allt 
▸ Löpande timräkjning är att föredra framför fastpris
▸ El och vatten-renoveringar ska man aldrig göra själv
▸ Där man tjänar mest pengar är på rivning och trädgårdsarbete
▸ Att köra skräp till tippen är också ett ställe där man kan spara bra pengar. 
▸ Var försiktig med offerttjänster som ofta blir ett "race-to-bottom"-scenario där de duktiga ▸ hantverkarna sällan deltar och de som är billigast har sällan tid att göra jobbet bäst. 
▸ Jämför inte bara på pris. Kvalité lönar sig.
▸ Avsätt tio procent av projektsumman som buffert för det du inte förutsett.
▸ Vi går även genom vad som är värt och renovera / investera i hemma

Vi hoppas att du gillar avsnittet,
Jan, Caroline och Christopher

=========
Reklam: slipp hantverksstrul, få hjälp och rådgivning via video med Comfy Living+
=========
Jag gillar enkelheten och kvaliteten på hjälpen vi har fått. I korthet fungerar Comfy som en app / hemsida där man lägger upp sin fråga. Därefter blir man kontaktad och rätt hantverkare bokas in. Vi har haft både snickare, plattsättare och elektriker hemma hos oss. 

Vi har valt att ha det som heter Comfy+. Det är att man betalar 79 kr per månad och då får man prioritet (eftersom oftast hos när man väl behöver anlita en hantverkare, då vill man ofta ha det gjort igår). Dessa 79 kr räknas sedan av mot fakturan så i praktiken betalar man inte för tjänsten. Christopher bjuder dig som är RT-medlem på sex månaders prov på Comfy+.

Läs mer:
https://comfyliving.se/rikatillsammans

=========
Innehållsförteckning
=========

I avsnittet kommer vi in på några av hans erfarenheter men han ger även en hel del tips på vad man kan tänka på när man renoverar själv eller anlitar hantverkare: 

▸ En bra tumregel är att räkna ca 1 000 kronor i timmen inklusive allt 
▸ Löpande timräkjning är att föredra framför fastpris
▸ El och vatten-renoveringar ska man aldrig göra själv
▸ Där man tjänar mest pengar är på rivning och trädgårdsarbete
▸ Att köra skräp till tippen är också ett ställe där man kan spara bra pengar. 
▸ Var försiktig med offerttjänster som ofta blir ett "race-to-bottom"-scenario där de duktiga ▸ hantverkarna sällan deltar och de som är billigast har sällan tid att göra jobbet bäst. 
▸ Jämför inte bara på pris. Kvalité lönar sig.
▸ Avsätt tio procent av projektsumman som buffert för det du inte förutsett.
▸ Vi går även genom vad som är värt och renovera / investera i hemma

Vi hoppas att du gillar avsnittet,
Jan, Caroline och Christopher

Reklam: slipp hantverksstrul, få hjälp och rådgivning via video med Comfy Living+
=========
Jag gillar enkelheten och kvaliteten på hjälpen vi har fått. I korthet fungerar Comfy som en app / hemsida där man lägger upp sin fråga. Därefter blir man kontaktad och rätt hantverkare bokas in. Vi har haft både snickare, plattsättare och elektriker hemma hos oss. 

Vi har valt att ha det som heter Comfy+. Det är att man betalar 79 kr per månad och då får man prioritet (eftersom oftast hos när man väl behöver anlita en hantverkare, då vill man ofta ha det gjort igår). Dessa 79 kr räknas sedan av mot fakturan så i praktiken betalar man inte för tjänsten. Christopher bjuder dig som är RT-medlem på sex månaders prov på Comfy+.

videos.title: The Key to Sharper, Evasive Turns
videos.summary_source_text:
The Key to Sharper, Evasive Turns The Downhill Skating System is the mechanics-first approach that unlocks effortless, controlled speed on the ice without extra conditioning, pushing or “trying harder.” Inspired by the movement signatures of players like Connor McDavid, Nathan MacKinnon, Cale Makar, Quinn Hughes, and other elite NHL skaters, this system teaches you how to move on the ice with gravity, using your body's own stretch shortening cycles mixed with the most efficient footwork patterns and various skating mechanics.

Most players skate “uphill”: stiff, blocky, pushing hard, creating tension and burning energy like we were always taught in traditional powerskating. Downhill skating flips that model. By using counter rotation, proper joint angles, and natural gravitational momentum, we teach you move faster with less effort.

Inside the Downhill Skating System, players learn to:

1) Unlock the inner spring for better acceleration.
2)Use different footwork patterns to add options, deception and effortlessness. 
3)Proper joint alignment for efficiency and balance instead of creating tension with push strides.

Apply NHL-base mechanics like shin angle, Y-angle, rhythm and cadence. Generate speed using the rocker, with heel pressure and subtle weight transfers.

This system is not what players would learn in traditional, outdated power skating methods. It’s a biomechanics-based operating system designed to match your body type and natural movement patterns.

Whether you’re trying to improve the forward stride, lateral movements, deception, or posture, Downhill Skating reveals the hidden mechanics the NHL’s best rely on, and shows you how to plug them into your game step by step.

If you’re ready to skate faster with less effort, flow through transitions, and move with the smoothness of the world’s best players, the Downhill Skating System is your blueprint to faster player development.

videos.summary_source_text:
Tap These 3 Spots for 30 Seconds — Feel What Happens to Your Body | Dr. Mandell Stress can affect nearly every system in your body, from your sleep and digestion to muscle tension, energy, focus, and overall well-being. In this video, Dr. Alan Mandell demonstrates a simple tapping routine using six areas around the jaw, cheeks, temples, forehead, top of the head, and base of the skull. Gentle rhythmic tapping provides sensory stimulation that may help you slow down, release some of the tension you’ve been carrying, and encourage a calmer state. Spend about 20 seconds at each area while breathing comfortably and paying attention to how your face, jaw, head, neck, and body begin to feel. This is an easy technique you can practice when you’re feeling tense, overwhelmed, before going to sleep, or anytime you simply need a moment to reset. Try the entire sequence and notice how you feel when you finish. Practice it regularly if you find it helpful, and share this video with someone who could use a little more calm in their day. Elon Musk’s 10 Trillion Parameter Grok 5 — Is This AGI? https://bitbiased.ai/ai-automation-services
Elon Musk says Grok 5 could be “indistinguishable from AGI.” But how much do we actually know about xAI’s next major AI model — and how much is hype?

In this video, we break down everything currently known about Grok 5: Musk’s claims about a massive 6–10 trillion parameter model, the enormous compute infrastructure behind it, SpaceX engineering data, Grok’s potential multimodal and agent capabilities, and how it could extend beyond the chatbot into Tesla Optimus, X, Starlink, and the wider Musk ecosystem.

But there’s a bigger problem for Grok 5: the AI race isn’t standing still. We also examine how the competitive bar has moved and what Grok 5 would actually need to accomplish to live up to Musk’s AGI claims.

Most importantly, we separate three things that often get mixed together: what has actually been confirmed, what has only been reported secondhand, and what remains speculation.

videos.summary_source_text:
New Audi A2: here’s what I LOVED and HATED! The Audi A2 is BACK… But is it as groundbreaking as the original? 

Explore new and used car deals with Carwow: https://bit.ly/Change-Your-Car-0709

Introducing the all-new Audi A2 e-tron! 

Audi has brought back the A2, and it’s set to replace the Audi A1 and Audi Q2! 

The question is: can this all-new Audi live up to the reputation of the original A2? And does it offer enough appeal over competitors like the Kia EV3 and Volvo EX30? Let’s take a closer look, starting with the design… 

Just like the original A2, the new model is relatively aerodynamic. Up front there’s a large, smooth panel that houses all of the safety driving features, and there are vents on either side of this to help smooth airflow around the car. There’s also a vent within the front bumper which can close to further help aero. Along the side you’ll find door handles similar to those on a Ferrari Purosangue, as well as more vents around the wheels and aero alloy wheels. Around the back, the similarities to the old car continue, along with large swooping taillights, a smart (and thin) Audi badge, coupled with a fake diffuser. 

On the inside, the main feature is the same swooping digital dial & infotainment screen - the same as found in any new Audi in 2026. Generally, materials are ok higher up in the cabin, with some cheaper plastics found when you reach lower down - although that’s to be expected with a car at this price point. Storage is ok throughout, and the seats are comfortable, with sports seats and Alcantara material available should you want it. The cupholder positioning can be moved, and there are buttons to open the door rather than traditional handles. 

The new Audi A2 e-tron will be available with 52, 61 and 84kWh battery packs. The entry-level car comes with 170hp & 350Nm, rising all the way to 326hp and 545Nm for the top-of-the-range model. The A2 offers ranges of 262 through to 401 miles, depending on which model you choose. 

The Audi A2 e-tron starts from £32,200, rising all the way up to £45,000 for the top-of-the-range model. This puts it slightly cheaper than the list price of its key competitors, but would you choose it over a Kia EV3 or Volvo EX30? Let us know in the comments!

6 Poop Facts That Will Shock You Believe it or not, your poop can tell you a lot about your health.

It’s one of the most direct indicators of what’s happening inside your digestive system.

🌟 Take the 2-minute Health Lever Quiz: https://drbrg.co/4gKEk8A

Just so you know, my full line of high-quality supplements is available on Amazon — search Dr. Berg Supplements.

And it can often point to potential issues long before they show up on other tests.

For example, if you notice your stool is thin, like a pencil or a cigar, that could signify a problem in your colon.

Small, hard pellets suggest something might be going on higher up in your digestive tract, perhaps affecting transit time.

And if your stool is consistently soft but not quite diarrhea, it might be an indication of missing gut microbes or even food allergies.

The color of your stool is also important. Light-colored or gray stool can point to a bile issue, which is produced by your liver and stored in your gallbladder.

If your stool has a bad odor and appears greasy, it might suggest a problem with your pancreas, as proper digestion of fats could be impaired.

It’s also important to know that it’s not normal to only have a bowel movement every 2 to 3 days. Ideally, you should have 1 to 2 bowel movements daily to ensure proper elimination.

Our bodies are constantly sending us signals like these.

Each one is a clue, guiding you toward what you truly need.

videos.title: Do This to Clean Your Ears the Right Way | Dr. Mandell
videos.summary_source_text:
Do This to Clean Your Ears the Right Way | Dr. Mandell Most people have used Q-tips to clean their ears for years, but what seems like a simple cleaning habit may actually push earwax deeper into the ear canal instead of removing it. In this video, Dr. Alan Mandell explains what can happen when wax becomes impacted near the eardrum, how it may affect hearing, ringing in the ears, dizziness, irritation, and infection risk, and why even the warning on the Q-tip box says not to insert the swab into the ear canal. You’ll also learn how your ears are designed to naturally move wax outward and the safer way to clean only the outer portion of the ear. If you’ve been using cotton swabs inside your ears, this is important information you’ll want to know and share with your family and friends. If you have persistent ear pain, hearing changes, drainage, dizziness, or other ear problems, always follow up with a qualified healthcare professional.

videos.title: Claude Fable 5.1 vs Gemini 3.8 Flash: This Isn’t Even Close
videos.summary_source_text:
Claude Fable 5.1 vs Gemini 3.8 Flash: This Isn’t Even Close Link to our newsletter: https://bitbiased.ai/

Anthropic and Google just released competing AI models one day apart — but the biggest difference isn't intelligence. It's price. Gemini 3.8 Flash is roughly 13x cheaper per token than Claude Fable 5.1, while Anthropic's model is claiming major gains in deep reasoning, coding, and long-duration agentic work.

On September 1, 2026, Anthropic announced Claude Fable 5.1, calling it its most capable model yet for coding and difficult knowledge work. The next day, Google launched Gemini 3.8 Flash alongside Flash Cyber, a specialized cybersecurity variant. Google says this was its third Flash release in just six weeks.

That release cadence alone shows how dramatically the AI race has accelerated.

On Anthropic's own benchmarks, Fable 5.1 more than doubled its predecessor's agentic science score from 24.7% to 52.6%, while agentic coding increased from 42% to 55.8%. On Anthropic's long-duration coding benchmark, Fable 5.1 reached 73.4%, ahead of Opus 5 at 70%.

Anthropic also cut cache read pricing by 75% to $0.25 per million tokens — an important change for AI agents that repeatedly call a model during long-running tasks. Fable 5.1 supports a one-million-token context window, text, images, PDFs, and diagrams, but not video or audio. Standard pricing sits at $10 per million input tokens and $50 per million output tokens.

Google took a very different approach.

Gemini 3.8 Flash launches at an introductory $0.75 per million input tokens and $3.75 per million output tokens. Google is competing on throughput and affordability without abandoning capability.

On DeepSWE, Gemini 3.8 Flash reportedly scored around 73.8%. Google's Harvey Legal Agent Benchmark increased from 8.8% with Gemini 3.7 Flash to 10.0%, while the specialized Flash Cyber model reportedly delivered a 2.6x improvement in correct patches on workloads from Google's Chrome security team.

Gemini 3.8 Flash also has a one-million-token context window, but supports text, images, PDFs, video, and audio — giving it an advantage for multimodal applications.

Head-to-head, the models represent two different strategies. Fable 5.1 appears stronger for deep multi-step reasoning, research-heavy work, and computer use, with Anthropic reporting a 77.9% partial-success score on OSWorld 2.0. Gemini 3.8 Flash reaches a reported 59.0%, up from 50.6% for Gemini 3.7 Flash.

But then there's the price gap.

At the announced rates, Gemini is roughly thirteen times cheaper per token. For a product processing 100 million tokens per day, the example explored in this video works out to roughly $6,000 per day with Fable 5.1 versus around $450 with Gemini 3.8 Flash.

For AI agents, that difference becomes even more important. Agents can make dozens or hundreds of model calls while planning, executing, testing, and correcting their work. Lower inference costs don't just make existing workflows cheaper — they can make entirely different levels of agentic computation economically practical.

Goldman Sachs projects AI-agent token consumption could increase 24x by 2030, while inference costs continue falling rapidly. If that trend holds, the winning AI model may not necessarily be the smartest one. It may be the model that's capable enough, fast enough, and cheap enough to run at enormous scale.

There's also an important limitation to this comparison: the benchmark numbers discussed here come from the companies themselves. At launch, there's no meaningful independent third-party verification directly comparing Fable 5.1 and Gemini 3.8 Flash under identical conditions.

So which one wins?

For deep research, complex reasoning, computer use, and demanding coding workflows, Fable 5.1 makes a strong case based on the reported results. For high-volume AI agents, multimodal applications, and products where inference cost matters at scale, Gemini 3.8 Flash becomes extremely difficult to ignore.

And that may be the real story: the AI race is shifting from finding one universally "best" model toward choosing the right model for the job.

videos.title: STOP, You're Training Your Biceps All Wrong!
videos.summary_source_text:
STOP, You're Training Your Biceps All Wrong! If you want to know how to build bigger biceps, how to get bigger biceps, or how to build big biceps that look thicker from every angle, this video shows you why simply doing more curls may not be the answer. You can perform barbell curls, dumbbell curls, preacher curls, hammer curls and cable curls every week, but if the mechanics are wrong, you can still leave biceps growth on the table.

Get the exact workouts and programs used by physical therapist Jeff Cavaliere here - https://athleanx.com
Subscribe To This Channel Here - http://bit.ly/2b0coMW

The biceps are not just elbow flexors. The biceps brachii also plays an important role in supinating the forearm, which means turning the palm upward. If you ignore that function and simply move a weight from the bottom of a curl to the top, you may be completing the rep without getting everything you can out of the muscle you are trying to build.

In this video, I break down the most common biceps training mistakes that can keep your arms from growing and show you how to fix the way you perform your curls.

One of the biggest mistakes is allowing other muscles to dominate the curl. When the shoulders drift forward, the elbows travel too far, the wrists bend excessively or momentum starts swinging the weight, the biceps can lose the tension you thought you were creating. Heavy curls are not automatically bad, but using more weight only helps if the target muscle is still doing the work.

Whether you are doing a barbell curl or dumbbell curl, think beyond simply getting the weight to your shoulders. Keep the tension where it belongs, control the eccentric on the way down, and use a range of motion that lets you challenge the biceps without turning the movement into a full-body exercise.

Supination is another major piece of building bigger biceps. If you are using dumbbells, actively turn the palm up as you raise the weight and continue trying to supinate near the top. This helps you train one of the true functions of the biceps instead of treating every curl like nothing more than elbow flexion.

Grip position can also change what you feel. A hammer curl is a great arm exercise, but it shifts more emphasis toward the brachialis and brachioradialis because the forearm stays in a neutral position. Those muscles matter for bigger arms, but if your goal is maximum biceps development, you still need curls that allow you to aggressively supinate the forearm.

Shoulder position matters too. The long head of the biceps crosses the shoulder joint, so where your upper arm sits changes the position of the muscle. Incline dumbbell curls challenge the biceps with the arm behind the body, while other curl variations place the arm more in front of the torso. A complete biceps workout should not rely on one curl angle forever.

You also want to stop ignoring the eccentric portion of your biceps exercises. It is easy to focus entirely on curling the weight up and then let it fall back down. Instead, control the lowering portion of every rep. The negative is another opportunity to keep tension on the biceps and make the set more productive.

Progressive overload matters, but overload is only useful when you are progressively overloading the muscle you intended to train. If every increase in weight causes more hip drive, shoulder movement and swinging, you may be getting better at moving the weight without getting better at training your biceps.

This is especially important if your biceps are not growing despite plenty of arm training. Before adding more sets of curls, look at how you are performing the sets you already have. Better biceps training often comes from better execution, exercise selection, stronger supination, controlled eccentrics and keeping tension on the biceps through the rep.

The takeaway is simple: stop judging a biceps exercise only by how much weight you can curl. Judge it by how effectively you can load the biceps, maintain tension, use the functions of the muscle and progressively challenge those mechanics over time. When you clean up your curl form, the same exercises can suddenly feel completely different.

If your biceps have stopped growing, your arms look flat from the front, or you simply want to know the best way to build bigger biceps, start with the fixes shown in this video. You do not necessarily need more biceps exercises. You need to get more out of the right ones.

videos.title: 10 Prompts That Prove Gemini 3.8 Flash Is Next Level
videos.summary_source_text:
10 Prompts That Prove Gemini 3.8 Flash Is Next Level Link to our newsletter: https://bitbiased.ai/

Gemini 3.8 Flash scored nine points higher than 3.7 on one of Google’s coding benchmarks — but if you prompt it the same way you prompt every other AI model, you may barely notice the upgrade.

The biggest changes aren’t about fancy prompt engineering. Gemini 3.8 Flash is specifically better at finishing multi-step jobs, checking its own work, handling massive amounts of context, and operating more like an agent instead of stopping at the first plausible answer. The trick is knowing how to prompt those capabilities directly.

Released on September 2nd, 2026, just three weeks after Gemini 3.7 Flash, Google is positioning 3.8 Flash as its intelligent workhorse for coding, long-horizon reasoning, and autonomous agents. The benchmark improvements help explain why: DeepSWE reportedly climbed from roughly 65% to 74%, while TerminalBench jumped from around 82% to 91%.

And Google is pricing Gemini 3.8 Flash at under $1 per million input tokens, making the model particularly interesting for workloads where you need AI running repeatedly rather than answering an occasional question.

But those improvements don’t show up equally everywhere.

In this video, I break down the practical prompts that actually expose what Gemini 3.8 Flash is good at — without complicated prompt frameworks or massive system instructions.

We start with coding and one surprisingly important change: asking Gemini to test and fix its work before returning the final result. Instead of simply asking it to write code, you can define “done” as producing something that has already been checked. That plays directly into the model’s improvements on longer, multi-step tasks.

Then there’s reasoning. Gemini 3.8 Flash offers low, medium, and high thinking levels, with medium as the default. For problems involving real math, logic, or multi-part decisions, explicitly requesting high effort and step-by-step reasoning can make much more sense than using extra computation on a trivial question.

Current information is another important boundary. The script notes a training-data cutoff around March 2026, so for newer developments, asking Gemini to use web search can help ground the response in current sources instead of relying on model memory. That still doesn’t remove the need to verify the sources it provides.

We also look at prompting Gemini 3.8 Flash for multi-step planning: mapping dependencies, identifying tasks that require earlier work to be completed, and flagging decisions that need human approval rather than letting the model quietly make every assumption itself.

Then there’s context. With a context window exceeding one million tokens, Gemini 3.8 Flash can work with enormous transcripts and documents without forcing you to chop everything into tiny pieces. That opens up useful workflows like extracting action items, owners, and deadlines from an entire long meeting transcript in one pass.

Gemini 3.8 Flash is multimodal too, accepting images, video, audio, and PDFs as input. But there’s an important limitation: this model analyzes those inputs and responds with text; it isn’t itself an image, video, or audio generator.

And 3.8 isn’t better at everything. On Humanity’s Last Exam, the script notes a score of roughly 45%, essentially unchanged from 3.7. The biggest improvements appear concentrated around coding and structured multi-step work rather than every form of open-ended reasoning.

So the real lesson isn’t to make your prompts longer. It’s to define what “finished” means: test the code, check the answer, search for current information when needed, plan the entire task, and use the full context you have available.

Try one of your normal Gemini prompts twice — once normally, and once with an explicit instruction to check or test its answer before finishing — and compare what comes back.

CHAPTERS

00:00 The Gemini 3.8 Flash Prompting Difference
01:17 What Actually Changed, And Why It Decides Your Prompts
02:49 Getting It To Actually Finish The Job Instead Of Stopping Halfway
04:11 Getting It To Check Its Work Instead Of Guessing
05:17 Getting It To Pull Current Information Instead Of Guessing From Memory
06:19 Getting It To Plan Multi-Step Tasks Instead Of Answering One Piece At A Time
07:23 Getting It To Handle The Big Stuff Without Chopping It Up
08:25 Getting It To Actually Look At What You Hand It
09:25 Where It Still Falls Short
10:13 The Verdict

videos.summary_source_text:
Stop Copying McDavid's Workout. Do This Instead. | The Train 2.0 Show Stop Copying McDavid's Workout. Do This Instead. | The Train 2.0 Show

Most hockey players build their summer around a program they saw an NHL player post, and then wonder why they show up to camp slower, tighter, or hurt. In this episode Kevin McKinnon, Train 2.0's Director of Coaching, sits down in person with Mason Hackel, a certified Train 2.0 coach and level three ATG coach out of Ann Arbor, to talk about the training philosophy he used to fix his own hips and what it looks like when you build it for a hockey player.

They get into the three lifts Mason builds every program around and the exact bodyweight standard he works players toward, the reason so many players tear an Achilles in the offseason and never see it coming, what to do about knee pain and hip pain before you touch anything explosive, the off-ice work that widens your corkscrew, one number in the gym that tracks directly with skating speed, and the order Kevin periodizes a summer so you peak at training camp instead of in July.

Watch the full episode for the standards, the demos, and the plan.

👉 Find Mason and every certified Train 2.0 coach on the coaches map: https://train2point0.com/coaches
👉 Mason Hackel: https://ability-training.com | Instagram: https://www.instagram.com/hockey_hacks_2.0/

The Downhill Skating System is the mechanics-first approach that unlocks effortless, controlled speed on the ice without extra conditioning, pushing or “trying harder.” Inspired by the movement signatures of players like Connor McDavid, Nathan MacKinnon, Cale Makar, Quinn Hughes, and other elite NHL skaters, this system teaches you how to move on the ice with gravity, using your body's own stretch shortening cycles mixed with the most efficient footwork patterns and various skating mechanics.

Most players skate “uphill”: stiff, blocky, pushing hard, creating tension and burning energy like we were always taught in traditional powerskating. Downhill skating flips that model. By using counter rotation, proper joint angles, and natural gravitational momentum, we teach you move faster with less effort.

Inside the Downhill Skating System, players learn to:

1) Unlock the inner spring for better acceleration.
2)Use different footwork patterns to add options, deception and effortlessness. 
3)Proper joint alignment for efficiency and balance instead of creating tension with push strides.

Apply NHL-base mechanics like shin angle, Y-angle, rhythm and cadence. Generate speed using the rocker, with heel pressure and subtle weight transfers.

This system is not what players would learn in traditional, outdated power skating methods. It’s a biomechanics-based operating system designed to match your body type and natural movement patterns.

Whether you’re trying to improve the forward stride, lateral movements, deception, or posture, Downhill Skating reveals the hidden mechanics the NHL’s best rely on, and shows you how to plug them into your game step by step.

If you’re ready to skate faster with less effort, flow through transitions, and move with the smoothness of the world’s best players, the Downhill Skating System is your blueprint to faster player development.

This system is not what players would learn in traditional, outdated power skating methods. It’s a biomechanics-based operating system designed to match your body type and natural movement patterns.

Whether you’re trying to improve the forward stride, lateral movements, deception, or posture, Downhill Skating reveals the hidden mechanics the NHL’s best rely on, and shows you how to plug them into your game step by step.

videos.summary_source_text:
Cover the Lead Side Like This  #golfswing #golftips To compress the ball well, your body needs to be preparing for impact earlier than most golfers realize. By allowing the lead shoulder to cover the lead leg and moving cohesively—shifting and turning together—you arrive at the impact line sooner and with more control. Using an alignment stick against the lead hip gives a clear visual of where impact should be and how early you can get there. This creates a smoother transition and much more consistent contact.

videos.title: Drink This Every Morning — Watch What Happens to Inflammation!  Dr. Mandell
videos.summary_source_text:
Drink This Every Morning — Watch What Happens to Inflammation!  Dr. Mandell Chronic inflammation can quietly affect the body over time, and this simple morning drink brings together ingredients that have been extensively studied for their antioxidant and anti-inflammatory properties. All you need is ¼ teaspoon of turmeric, 1 tablespoon of extra-virgin olive oil, 1 cup of warm water, a pinch of black pepper, and, if desired, a squeeze of fresh orange juice. To prepare it, first mix the turmeric with the extra-virgin olive oil, then add 1 cup of warm water and stir well. Sprinkle in a small pinch of black pepper and, if you prefer a little additional flavor, squeeze in some fresh orange juice. Drink this first thing in the morning before breakfast on an empty stomach; you can also enjoy it at another time during the day. Turmeric contains curcumin, a naturally occurring compound that has been widely researched for its effects on inflammatory signaling and oxidative stress. Extra-virgin olive oil supplies healthy monounsaturated fats and protective polyphenols, while its fat content also helps with the absorption of curcumin. Black pepper contains piperine, which can substantially increase curcumin's bioavailability, allowing the body to utilize more of it. Together, these ingredients create a simple nutritional combination that can complement an overall anti-inflammatory lifestyle. Remember, no single drink can erase or cure chronic inflammation, but what you consistently put into your body can influence your overall health. Combine good nutrition with regular movement, adequate sleep, hydration, stress management, and other healthy lifestyle choices. If you take medications or have a medical condition, particularly if you use blood-thinning medication or have gallbladder problems, speak with your healthcare professional before making turmeric a regular part of your routine. videos.title: Elon Musk’s “Macrohard” Is Supposed to Launch THIS MONTH
videos.summary_source_text:
Elon Musk’s “Macrohard” Is Supposed to Launch THIS MONTH Link to our newsletter: https://bitbiased.ai/

Elon Musk says Macrohard is still on track for a September 2026 launch. That deadline is now here — but behind the scenes, xAI’s ambitious “purely AI software company” has reportedly lost leaders, shed engineers, paused a roughly 600-person data operation, and effectively started over.

Macrohard began as a joke aimed at Microsoft. Musk teased the project in July 2025 as a “multi-agent AI software company,” and xAI filed a US trademark for the Macrohard name in August. Musk’s premise was surprisingly straightforward: because a company like Microsoft primarily produces software rather than physical hardware, its workflows could theoretically be simulated by AI agents.

The vision goes far beyond another Copilot. Musk described Grok spawning specialized coding and image agents capable of coordinating their work and evaluating outputs. In March 2026, he revealed more of the architecture: Grok would serve as the high-level “navigator,” while a Tesla-built agent watches a computer screen, clicks, types, and operates software like a human. Musk calls the combination Digital Optimus.

That immediately raised a bigger question: what happens if AI agents stop being assistants and start functioning as the workers themselves?

The economics help explain why Wall Street paid attention. A mid-level engineer can cost roughly $120,000 per year, while an Nvidia H100 GPU reportedly rents for around $3–$10 per hour. Behind xAI sits the enormous Colossus cluster in Memphis, reportedly containing more than 180,000 Nvidia GPUs. Macrohard also emerged as Anthropic pushed further into autonomous office work with Claude Cowork and Microsoft expanded Copilot across its ecosystem.

But the public pitch and the story unfolding inside xAI soon started looking very different.

Reports described Macrohard as stalled. Two leaders left in February. xAI co-founder Toby Pohlen was brought in to take over — and reportedly lasted just 16 days. More than 20 engineers publicly associated with Macrohard reportedly either left xAI or transferred elsewhere.

Then came another major setback: a data-labeling operation involving roughly 600 outside contractors was reportedly paused. Meanwhile, Tesla was developing its own computer-using agent, also unofficially called Digital Optimus, creating two teams inside Musk’s empire pursuing closely related ideas.

Musk responded by rebuilding. On March 12, xAI hired two senior engineers from Cursor, with both reporting directly to Musk. A day later, Musk acknowledged that Macrohard simply “wasn’t built right the first time.”

There’s also a wider xAI story underneath all of this. Roughly half of the company’s original 11 co-founders were reportedly gone, while some reporting put the SpaceX-integrated AI division’s operating loss above $2.5 billion for a single quarter. xAI has also reportedly leased excess Colossus capacity to competitors including Google and Anthropic.

One important distinction: some coverage initially characterized the Cursor move as an acquisition. What’s confirmed here is the hiring of two executives — not xAI purchasing Cursor.

Now September 2026 has arrived.

The Macrohard trademark is real. Musk has publicly described the architecture. xAI has continued recruiting for roles connected to the project, including AI agent testing and data-labeling jobs reportedly paying up to $40 per hour.

What we still don’t have is a working public demo, a shipped public product, or independent verification that the rebuilt team has solved the coordination and reliability problems that reportedly derailed the first version.

So does Musk actually deliver Macrohard this month? Do we get a full public launch, a limited release designed to technically hit the deadline, another delay — or nothing at all?

This video reconstructs the full Macrohard story and separates what’s confirmed from what remains a promise.

01:33 The Pitch
03:21 Why Wall Street Flinched
05:29 The Story Nobody Announced
07:37 Starting Over, Again
09:41 The September Deadline
11:19 The Verdict

videos.title: OpenAI cuts off Musk, Anthropic BEATS Pentagon, Grok could go DARK: AI NEWS
videos.summary_source_text:
OpenAI cuts off Musk, Anthropic BEATS Pentagon, Grok could go DARK: AI NEWS Link to our newsletter: https://bitbiased.ai/

OpenAI is reportedly cutting off model access to Cursor after SpaceX announced a $60 billion acquisition of Anysphere. A federal judge just ruled that the Pentagon’s blacklisting of Anthropic was illegal and baseless. And xAI has warned a court that an environmental dispute over gas turbines could cause Grok to largely cease functioning for hundreds of millions of users.

Three stories that look completely unrelated are really asking the same question: who actually controls whether an AI model gets to keep running?

The first fight centers on Cursor, the AI coding tool built by Anysphere. After SpaceX announced it was acquiring the company in a deal reportedly worth $60 billion, OpenAI moved to cut off Cursor’s access to its models, with the cutoff scheduled for November 12. According to the reporting discussed in this video, OpenAI’s justification involves distrust of Musk-connected companies alongside alleged terms-of-service violations tied to xAI.

But that explanation has two very different layers. A terms-of-service violation is something concrete. Distrust of companies connected to Elon Musk is much broader. And when the decision arrives within days of one of OpenAI’s best-funded competitors acquiring Cursor, the move becomes more than a simple compliance story.

There is also an important limitation: we do not yet have a public, itemized breakdown showing exactly which terms were allegedly violated and when. That makes this potentially both a policy enforcement decision and a strategic competitive move.

Then there is Anthropic.

Earlier in 2026, the Department of Defense pushed Anthropic to remove two restrictions governing military use of Claude: its prohibition on autonomous weapons selecting targets without human involvement and its prohibition on mass domestic surveillance of Americans. Anthropic refused.

The Pentagon subsequently designated Anthropic under a federal statute that legal experts described as having never previously been used against a domestic American company and as normally being associated with foreign sabotage threats. Anthropic sued in March.

Now a federal judge has ruled that the Pentagon’s blacklisting of Anthropic was illegal and baseless.

That could reopen the path toward military contracts potentially worth billions, but it does not mean those contracts automatically return. The Pentagon can still appeal, and existing arrangements involving competitors including OpenAI and xAI remain unaffected. What changed is Anthropic’s legal position after months of fighting one of the most powerful customers in the world over how Claude could be used.

And then the third story moves from model access and military policy to something much more physical: electricity.

xAI is facing a Clean Air Act lawsuit involving gas turbines at a Mississippi power site that the suit alleges were not properly permitted. Those turbines help support the compute infrastructure behind Grok.

In a federal court filing, xAI argued that shutting down that power source could cause Grok to largely cease functioning for hundreds of millions of users.

That is an enormous claim, but it needs context. It comes from xAI itself during active litigation in which the company is attempting to avoid an injunction. It should therefore be understood as a legal argument rather than an independently verified assessment that Grok is actually on the verge of going offline.

Put all three stories together and the bigger pattern becomes clear.

OpenAI can control access to the models another company depends on. Anthropic just fought over how much leverage the Pentagon can exercise over an AI provider that refuses certain uses of its technology. And xAI is arguing that regulators’ control over physical power infrastructure could ultimately determine whether Grok stays available.

Same lever. Three different hands trying to hold it.

The most important AI battles may increasingly have less to do with benchmark scores and model capabilities and more to do with access agreements, government contracts, courts, infrastructure, electricity, and who ultimately controls the switch.

And none of these stories is finished yet. The Cursor cutoff has not taken effect. The Pentagon can still appeal the Anthropic ruling. And xAI’s turbine dispute remains in litigation.

The models themselves may not have changed this week. The power structures determining whether people can use them did.

03:49 The Court Just Overturned the Pentagon Ban
06:02 xAI Says Grok Could Go Dark
08:00 What Actually Connects These Three Stories

10:11 The Verdict

videos.title: The Golf Swing Becomes Effortless When You Understand This
videos.summary_source_text:
The Golf Swing Becomes Effortless When You Understand This Ever wondered why your golf swing can feel so difficult… when your body is actually capable of producing an incredible golf swing naturally?

I recently came across a video from Christian Cee  that stopped me in my tracks.

One moment he was making a fairly typical amateur golf swing. Seconds later, without even realising it, he produced a movement that looked remarkably similar to some of the best golfers in the world.

The interesting part?

Nobody taught him how to do it.

In this golf lesson, Danny Maude reveals why Christian’s accidental “tour level” movement happened — and what it can teach you about creating a more natural, powerful and effortless golf swing.

Most golfers spend their time trying to control individual parts of the swing.

Where should my hands go?
How should my hips move?
Am I shifting my weight correctly?
Where should the club be at impact?

But your body is incredibly good at organising movement when you give it a clear enough task.

Christian accidentally demonstrated this perfectly.

He created weight shift, rotation, extension, speed and a powerful release without consciously trying to manufacture any of them.

The challenge is learning how to bring that same freedom into your golf swing… while still controlling the clubface and striking the golf ball consistently.

In this video you’ll discover:

• Why Christian accidentally created a golf swing that looked like a tour professional
• How your body naturally organises movement around a clear task
• Why focusing too much on the golf ball can actually make your swing worse
• The difference between your primary and secondary targets in the golf swing
• How to combine freedom with control
• A simple ball throwing drill inspired by Pete Cowen
• How to improve your strike without becoming obsessed with impact
• Why trying to “control” your golf swing can often make you lose control
• A simple stepping exercise that can help develop a more natural golf swing
• How to build trust and create effortless speed through impact

The goal isn’t to stop caring about your strike.

It’s to stop making the golf ball the master of your entire movement.

When you learn to connect what’s happening at impact with where you actually want the golf club and golf ball to go, the swing can start to organise itself very differently.

And often, many of the movements golfers spend years trying to manufacture begin to appear naturally.

Statin medications are the most commonly prescribed drug class in the United States, yet most people are unaware of their potential side effects.

Statins are typically prescribed when cholesterol levels are high. They block the production of cholesterol, but they also block the production of CoQ10, which is vital for muscle and heart health.

If you’re taking statins, CoQ10 can help mitigate the side effects. Ubiquinol is a fast-acting form of CoQ10 and may be the best form to take. A typical amount is 200–400 mg.

Instead of immediately taking statins, ask yourself: Why do you have high cholesterol in the first place? Refined carbohydrates and sugar can contribute to cholesterol production in the body. Low bile, gallbladder problems, or gallbladder removal can also contribute to high cholesterol.

videos.title: 1,100hp M2 v Lambo Huracan Perf: DRAG RACE
videos.summary_source_text:
1,100hp M2 v Lambo Huracan Perf: DRAG RACE Does a RWD Red Bull drift car have what it takes to beat an AWD Lambo in a straight line?!

Explore new and used car deals with Carwow: https://bit.ly/Change-Your-Car-0509

It’s time for a drag race with one of the craziest M2s we’ve ever seen!

We’ve got our hands on a Red Bull BMW M2 - and it’s been converted into a drift car! So we’re going to see if a car that’s made for cornering at extreme speed has what it takes to beat a Lamborghini in a straight line!

Does it stand a chance? Let’s take a closer look at the stats…

The Red Bull M2 is powered by a BMW S58 engine. However, rather than having twin turbos, this 3-litre straight-six instead comes with one single (yet massive!) turbo, and the power output has been increased to an incredible 1,100hp and 1,200Nm! All of this power is sent to the rear wheels only via a 5-speed sequential gearbox, and being a drift car, it’s super light, tipping the scales at around 1,400kg.

As for the Lambo, it’s the Huracan Performante! That means it’s powered by a 5.2-litre naturally-aspirated V10 that delivers 640hp and 600Nm. 04.09.26 - RIFT Education Day RIFT is a modern trading platform that combines automated trading, manual trading, futures trading, and educational tools into one ecosystem.

Designed for both beginners and experienced traders, RIFT aims to simplify access to financial markets while providing users with tools that can help them participate more efficiently.

One of the key features of RIFT is its Auto Trading Engine, which allows users to allocate capital into automated trading strategies designed to operate without the need for constant monitoring. This enables participants to remain active in the markets without spending hours each day analyzing charts or placing trades manually.

For users who prefer direct market participation, RIFT also offers Manual Trading and Futures Trading functionality. This gives traders the flexibility to execute their own strategies, manage positions, and take advantage of market opportunities in real time.

RIFT is built around a non-custodial philosophy, meaning users maintain control of their own funds rather than depositing them into a centralized company account. This approach aligns with the growing demand for greater transparency, security, and user control within the digital asset industry.

Beyond trading, RIFT focuses heavily on education. Through training sessions, community support, and ongoing learning resources, users can develop a deeper understanding of trading, risk management, market psychology, and financial technology.

The platform also incorporates modern technologies such as AI-driven infrastructure, advanced execution systems, copy trading capabilities, and future integrations designed to create a more connected and intelligent trading environment.

Whether you are completely new to trading, looking for automated solutions, interested in futures markets, or seeking to expand your financial knowledge, RIFT aims to provide a complete ecosystem where users can learn, participate, and grow.

Instead of turning only your shoulders or lifting your arms, focus on moving from your chest to your belt buckle — using your ribcage to power the backswing.

This enables participants to remain active in the markets without spending hours each day analyzing charts or placing trades manually.

Longevity Secrets to Help You Live 100 Years Everyone wants to live a long, healthy life.

But what can you actually do to make that a reality?

🌟 Take the 2-minute Health Lever Quiz: https://drbrg.co/4xodMji

Just so you know, my full line of high-quality supplements is available on Amazon — search Dr. Berg Supplements.

It turns out there are some really practical, science-backed steps you can take.

For example, maintaining optimal vitamin D levels is crucial.

Many people think their levels are fine, but getting them regularly checked can reveal a different story.

And regular exercise isn’t just for weight management. It supports so many body functions that contribute to longevity.

Avoiding seed oils and excessive sugar is also key. These things can create metabolic stress that directly impacts your body’s ability to maintain healthy cells over time.

Think about cooking with herbs like parsley, thyme, oregano, and basil. They aren’t just for flavor; they’re packed with phytonutrients that can support your cells and overall well-being.

Intermittent fasting is another powerful tool. It helps your body repair and renew cells, essentially cleaning house at a cellular level.

And don’t underestimate the power of social connections. Research shows that fostering strong relationships can have a significant positive impact on how long and how well you live.

Eating fermented foods supports a healthy gut microbiome, which is foundational for nutrient absorption and immune function.

Drinking lemon water daily and taking post-meal walks are simple ways to support digestion and steady blood sugar levels.

Even avoiding cooking in iron skillets can make a difference for some, by helping to manage iron levels in the body.

And, of course, getting 7-9 hours of quality sleep every night is non-negotiable for repair, hormone balance, and overall vitality.

All of these choices can contribute to a long and healthy life.

But when it comes to supporting your overall health, it can be hard to know where to begin. Everyone’s body is different, and what works for one person may not work for another.

videos.title: 5 Default Posture Habits Every Hockey Player Should Develop
videos.summary_source_text:
5 Default Posture Habits Every Hockey Player Should Develop The Downhill Skating System is the mechanics-first approach that unlocks effortless, controlled speed on the ice without extra conditioning, pushing or “trying harder.” Inspired by the movement signatures of players like Connor McDavid, Nathan MacKinnon, Cale Makar, Quinn Hughes, and other elite NHL skaters, this system teaches you how to move on the ice with gravity, using your body's own stretch shortening cycles mixed with the most efficient footwork patterns and various skating mechanics.

Most players skate “uphill”: stiff, blocky, pushing hard, creating tension and burning energy like we were always taught in traditional powerskating. Downhill skating flips that model. By using counter rotation, proper joint angles, and natural gravitational momentum, we teach you move faster with less effort.

Inside the Downhill Skating System, players learn to:

1) Unlock the inner spring for better acceleration.
2)Use different footwork patterns to add options, deception and effortlessness. 
3)Proper joint alignment for efficiency and balance instead of creating tension with push strides.

Apply NHL-base mechanics like shin angle, Y-angle, rhythm and cadence. Generate speed using the rocker, with heel pressure and subtle weight transfers.

This system is not what players would learn in traditional, outdated power skating methods. It’s a biomechanics-based operating system designed to match your body type and natural movement patterns.

Whether you’re trying to improve the forward stride, lateral movements, deception, or posture, Downhill Skating reveals the hidden mechanics the NHL’s best rely on, and shows you how to plug them into your game step by step.

If you’re ready to skate faster with less effort, flow through transitions, and move with the smoothness of the world’s best players, the Downhill Skating System is your blueprint to faster player development.
