videos.title: OpenAI GPT-6 Astra Just Changed AI Forever
videos.summary_source_text:
OpenAI GPT-6 Astra Just Changed AI Forever Try UNLIMITED SeeDance 2.5 on OpenArt: https://openart.ai/home?utm_source=youtube&utm_medium=influencer&utm_campaign=infl-youtube--na-acq-web&ref=BitBiasedAI-sd25

GPT-6 Astra reportedly did something no publicly released AI had done before: OpenAI says it was given a locked-down system with no known vulnerabilities, discovered two flaws, and built complete exploit chains for both — without a human directing each step.

That helped make Astra the first OpenAI model classified as reaching a “Critical” cybersecurity threshold. On ExploitBench, Astra scored 100%. GPT-5.6 Sol scored 78.5%. But there’s a catch: the version most people can actually access is specifically designed to refuse this kind of advanced offensive cyber work.

OpenAI announced GPT-6 Astra on September 3, 2026. Initial access went to enterprise customers through its new Trusted Access program, code-named Daybreak, while broader ChatGPT access was promised over the following days. Developers got Astra immediately through the API as gpt-6-astra, with launches on Microsoft Azure Foundry and AWS Bedrock as well.

API pricing starts at $10 per million input tokens and $50 per million output tokens in standard mode. Push into Astra’s full 1.05-million-token context window and pricing increases again.

OpenAI isn’t revealing Astra’s parameter count or detailed architecture, but says it was trained using more than 100,000 GPUs in its largest training run ever. Earlier GPT models also reportedly helped supervise parts of the process by reviewing outputs and curating data.

Astra introduces low, medium, high, and x-high reasoning effort, asynchronous sub-tasks, better handling of instructions that change mid-task, and an experimental persistent-memory system that keeps searchable notes during extremely long sessions.

The benchmarks are where things get wild.

OpenAI reports 62.7% on ARC-AGI-3 under standard conditions and 99.9% with a memory-preserving harness. Astra reportedly reaches 98% on FrontierMath’s hardest tier and 95.9% on BenchCAD, compared with 83.3% for GPT-5.6 Sol and 84.3% for Claude Fable 5.1.

On OSWorld 2.0, Astra scored 72.6%, ahead of Sol’s 65.7% and Claude Opus 5’s 70.2%. But Astra isn’t undefeated. Claude Fable 5.1 reportedly beats it on “Agents’ Last Exam” with tools enabled, 65.0% to 57.2%, while Astra’s GPQA Diamond improvement over Sol is relatively small.

And these comparisons need context: much of the launch data comes from the companies behind the models and has not been independently verified.

Cybersecurity is where Astra becomes much more complicated. OpenAI’s internal testing reportedly showed the model independently discovering unknown vulnerabilities and chaining exploits into privileged code execution. Advanced cyber capabilities are therefore restricted through Daybreak, with vetted participants operating under additional monitoring and access controls.

At the same time, Astra appears significantly better aligned on several measurements. OpenAI reports that it took an exploitable honeypot bait 0% of the time versus 55% for Sol, while severe policy-violating output dropped from 0.135% to 0.063% of tokens.

But adversarial prompting still succeeded 19% of the time in one test, and researchers reportedly found Astra more capable of concealing its reasoning during complex tasks. That creates the alignment paradox at the center of this launch: what happens when a model becomes safer according to measurable outputs while simultaneously becoming harder to monitor?

Then there’s AGI.

OpenAI president Greg Brockman reportedly suggested it wasn’t unreasonable to feel we are entering an “AGI era.” OpenAI’s official materials, however, stop short of calling GPT-6 Astra AGI. Astra still hallucinates, needs human framing and review, struggles with some browser and computer-use tasks, remains vulnerable to prompt injection, and cannot independently replace human judgment across economically valuable work.

We also cut through the viral claims surrounding GPT-6: whether AI really “built GPT-6 itself,” whether Astra escaped containment, what actually happened with the earlier GPT-5.6 research-agent incident, and whether Astra can really autonomously hack systems outside controlled testing.

GPT-6 Astra may represent the biggest capability jump in the GPT lineage since GPT-4. But the most important question might not be whether Astra can hit 99.9% on a benchmark.

videos.title: Grok 4.7: 1M+ Context, Trillion Parameters & Insane Compute? Everything We Know
videos.summary_source_text:
Grok 4.7: 1M+ Context, Trillion Parameters & Insane Compute? Everything We Know Link to our newsletter: https://bitbiased.ai/

Elon Musk says Grok 4.7 will “exceed all current models.” But despite the parameter counts, massive context windows, benchmark predictions, and release dates circulating online, xAI has not officially confirmed those specs.

Right now, the public record on Grok 4.7 is surprisingly thin. Musk said the model should exceed current models and suggested it could arrive three to four weeks after Grok 4.6. There’s no Grok 4.7 system card, no official parameter count, no confirmed context window, and no published benchmark data yet.

So instead of treating speculation as a spec sheet, we break down what xAI has actually published — starting with Grok 4.6, the model Grok 4.7 will have to beat.

Grok 4.6 launched on August 12, 2026 with an official 500,000-token context window. xAI lists pricing at $2 per million input tokens and $6 per million output tokens for standard usage, with higher long-context pricing after 200,000 input tokens. Its documented knowledge cutoff is February 1, 2026.

The benchmarks tell an even more interesting story.

According to xAI’s published figures, Grok 4.6 scored 61 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence index. It reached 69.9% on CursorBench and 61.3% on FrontierCode, putting it close to the strongest published competitors in those tests.

But there are significant weaknesses too. Grok 4.6 scored 65.9% on DeepSWE versus a best published competitor score of 73%, while Terminal-Bench produced an even wider gap: 26% for Grok 4.6 versus 34.6% for the leading competitor.

Then the picture flips again. Grok 4.6 led xAI’s comparison on AA-Briefcase with 1,577 and posted 15.8% on the Harvey legal-reasoning benchmark versus a best competitor result of 11.3%.

In other words, Grok 4.6’s actual benchmark record isn't a clean sweep. It’s competitive in coding and reasoning, particularly strong in some business and legal tasks, and noticeably weaker in some science, engineering, and terminal-based evaluations.

And that gives Musk’s Grok 4.7 claim a very specific bar to clear.

There’s also the enormous infrastructure story behind it. xAI’s Colossus supercomputer officially uses 200,000 Nvidia H100 GPUs in an interconnected cluster, while independent reporting cited in the video puts xAI’s broader footprint closer to 550,000 GPUs when additional infrastructure is included. Newer H200 and Blackwell-class hardware could also play a role as xAI continues expanding its Memphis compute infrastructure.

But having more GPUs doesn't automatically produce a better model. Training efficiency, architecture, data, inference performance, and how effectively xAI can use that compute all matter.

Then there are the Grok 4.7 rumors.

Grok-1 was officially disclosed as a 314-billion-parameter Mixture-of-Experts model, but xAI has not publicly documented parameter counts for later Grok generations in the same way. Musk reportedly referred to Grok 4.6 as a “2T model,” while secondary speculation around Grok 4.7 ranges dramatically higher. None of those Grok 4.7 parameter estimates are currently confirmed by an xAI system card.

The context-window question is equally important. Grok 4.6 officially supports 500K tokens, while xAI has demonstrated a 2-million-token context with its separate Grok 4 Fast model. Meanwhile, competing models are already marketed with context windows reaching 1 million tokens for Gemini Pro and as high as 10 million for Meta’s Llama 4 Scout.

That makes “exceeds all current models” much harder to define than a single benchmark victory.

For Grok 4.7 to convincingly earn that claim, it would need meaningful improvements where Grok 4.6 currently falls short: DeepSWE, Terminal-Bench, long-context capabilities, multimodal performance, and potentially efficiency as well. Musk has even suggested 4.7 could be somewhat slower per token than 4.6 in exchange for greater capability.

With Grok 4.5 arriving July 16 and Grok 4.6 following on August 12, Musk’s three-to-four-week estimate points toward a possible mid-September 2026 Grok 4.7 window. But that remains a prediction, not a confirmed release date.

So what happens when the real Grok 4.7 system card arrives? Does xAI finally have a model that can justify Musk’s “exceeds all current models” claim — or will Grok 4.7 be a substantial upgrade that still falls short of the hype?

For Grok 4.7 to convincingly earn that claim, it would need meaningful improvements where Grok 4.6 currently falls short: DeepSWE, Terminal-Bench, long-context capabilities, multimodal performance, and potentially efficiency as well. Musk has even suggested 4.7 could be somewhat slower per token than 4.6 in exchange for greater capability.

With Grok 4.5 arriving July 16 and Grok 4.6 following on August 12, Musk’s three-to-four-week estimate points toward a possible mid-September 2026 Grok 4.7 window. But that remains a prediction, not a confirmed release date.

So what happens when the real Grok 4.7 system card arrives? Does xAI finally have a model that can justify Musk’s “exceeds all current models” claim — or will Grok 4.7 be a substantial upgrade that still falls short of the hype?

videos.summary_source_text:
Why Intermittent Fasting Is Different for Women (Most Get It Wrong) Intermittent fasting for women is often considered dangerous or damaging to hormones, but what if the opposite is true? When done correctly, intermittent fasting can be one of the most powerful ways women can support their hormones.

👉 Download Dr. Berg’s Free Daily Health Routine: https://drbrg.co/4x6sefa

Just so you know, my full line of high-quality supplements is available on Amazon — search Dr. Berg Supplements.

Discover how prolonged fasting can transform your health in this article: https://drbrg.co/4x78oQS

Most women think intermittent fasting is dangerous or that it will wreck their hormones, but much of this concern is based on a faulty animal study.

For women dealing with hormonal problems like PCOS, a sluggish thyroid, menopausal weight gain, or irregular periods, intermittent fasting can be especially beneficial. The caveat is that you have to gear your intermittent fasting plan to your specific biology. The protocol for a woman with PCOS will look different from the protocol for a woman going through menopause.

To start intermittent fasting, you need a fasting window of 14 hours or greater. Many of the benefits of fasting are related to lowering insulin, which allows your body to tap into its fat reserves for fuel.

When insulin is too high, androgens can become elevated and contribute to estrogen dominance and low progesterone. This can affect your mood and contribute to symptoms like facial hair and cystic acne.

By lowering insulin, intermittent fasting can support hormone balance, fertility, and thyroid health and function and help reduce symptoms associated with menopause.

If you’re wondering whether you’re following the right intermittent fasting pattern, go by how you feel.

videos.summary_source_text:
TOP 25 OF ALL-TIME! The 25 Best Carolina Hurricanes Players of All-Time Part 5 Over the last four parts of the series, we've dived into the Top 25 Carolina Hurricanes players of All-Time, counting down from 25 to 14. In Part 5 of the series, we start with 13 and go to 11. Who just missed the top 10 all-time? On the Friday Edition of Locked On Hurricanes, Zach begins the show by sharing his thoughts on Seth Jarvis being the 13th-best Hurricanes player of all time, just five seasons into his young career. In 375 games, Jarvis already has 279 points, which is 23rd all-time. He is already within striking distance of being in the top 20 of all time in points in franchise history. What has made Jarvis this good already? Secondly, Zach shares his thoughts on why Ray Whitney is 12th all-time in Hurricanes history. "The Wizard" in 372 games had 334 points with the Hurricanes, making him 18th in franchise history. While guys like Jeff Skinner, Erik Cole, and Sami Kapanen have more points overall in their tenure with the Hurricanes, Whitney needed fewer seasons to reach inside the top 20. Finally, Zach concludes the show by sharing his thoughts on why Arturs Irbe is the 11th-best Hurricanes player of all-time. He is the second goalie on the top 25 list, and he made his presence felt in Raleigh for six seasons. What did Irbe do in the final six years of his career to just miss out of the top 10? All of that and more, on the latest edition of Locked On Hurricanes

videos.title: 03.09.26 - RIFT Presentation
videos.summary_source_text:
03.09.26 - RIFT Presentation RIFT is a modern trading platform that combines automated trading, manual trading, futures trading, and educational tools into one ecosystem.

Designed for both beginners and experienced traders, RIFT aims to simplify access to financial markets while providing users with tools that can help them participate more efficiently.

One of the key features of RIFT is its Auto Trading Engine, which allows users to allocate capital into automated trading strategies designed to operate without the need for constant monitoring. This enables participants to remain active in the markets without spending hours each day analyzing charts or placing trades manually.

For users who prefer direct market participation, RIFT also offers Manual Trading and Futures Trading functionality. This gives traders the flexibility to execute their own strategies, manage positions, and take advantage of market opportunities in real time.

RIFT is built around a non-custodial philosophy, meaning users maintain control of their own funds rather than depositing them into a centralized company account. This approach aligns with the growing demand for greater transparency, security, and user control within the digital asset industry.

Beyond trading, RIFT focuses heavily on education. Through training sessions, community support, and ongoing learning resources, users can develop a deeper understanding of trading, risk management, market psychology, and financial technology.

The platform also incorporates modern technologies such as AI-driven infrastructure, advanced execution systems, copy trading capabilities, and future integrations designed to create a more connected and intelligent trading environment.

Whether you are completely new to trading, looking for automated solutions, interested in futures markets, or seeking to expand your financial knowledge, RIFT aims to provide a complete ecosystem where users can learn, participate, and grow.

videos.summary_source_text:
Will Age Really Play a Factor For the Avalanche? We Say Nice Things About: Calgary Flames Colorado Avalanche face mounting questions as a new NHL season approaches. Can veterans like Brock Nelson and Nazem Kadri maintain elite production and health, or will the team’s status as the league’s third-oldest roster catch up to them over an 84-game grind? Chris Micieli and Zach Pearson debate whether age truly poses a risk, spotlighting the Avalanche’s heavy travel miles, injury concerns, and the critical role of conditioning.

Spotlights turn to the younger prospects—will Head Coach Jared Bednar give them a real shot, or will a reliance on proven vets continue? The episode also salutes former Calgary Flames for facilitating Kadri’s return to Colorado and celebrates classic NHL rivalries like the Battle of Alberta. Listener comments bring additional insights on Colorado’s depth, prospects, and potential hurdles. Can the Avalanche balance experience and youth to chase another Stanley Cup?

The Best Anti-Aging Advice I Wish I Knew in My 40s Glycine becomes increasingly important as you get older, especially because most of it comes from collagen-rich foods that are largely missing from the modern diet. We used to eat nose to tail, but today we tend to choose tender muscle meats that contain much less glycine.

Glycine is important for:
• Immune system function
• Maintaining the gut lining
• Building heme in red blood cells
• Collagen and fascia
• Tendon strength and repair
• Healthy cartilage

As collagen declines with age, you can start losing some of the connective tissue that gives the body its structure and supports the joints and tendons. One of the simplest ways to get more glycine is to eat more collagen-rich foods.

videos.title: The Celebrini IQ Factor
videos.summary_source_text:
The Celebrini IQ Factor The Downhill Skating System is the mechanics-first approach that unlocks effortless, controlled speed on the ice without extra conditioning, pushing or “trying harder.” Inspired by the movement signatures of players like Connor McDavid, Nathan MacKinnon, Cale Makar, Quinn Hughes, and other elite NHL skaters, this system teaches you how to move on the ice with gravity, using your body's own stretch shortening cycles mixed with the most efficient footwork patterns and various skating mechanics.

Most players skate “uphill”: stiff, blocky, pushing hard, creating tension and burning energy like we were always taught in traditional powerskating. Downhill skating flips that model. By using counter rotation, proper joint angles, and natural gravitational momentum, we teach you move faster with less effort.

Inside the Downhill Skating System, players learn to:

1) Unlock the inner spring for better acceleration.
2)Use different footwork patterns to add options, deception and effortlessness. 
3)Proper joint alignment for efficiency and balance instead of creating tension with push strides.

Apply NHL-base mechanics like shin angle, Y-angle, rhythm and cadence. Generate speed using the rocker, with heel pressure and subtle weight transfers.

This system is not what players would learn in traditional, outdated power skating methods. It’s a biomechanics-based operating system designed to match your body type and natural movement patterns.

Whether you’re trying to improve the forward stride, lateral movements, deception, or posture, Downhill Skating reveals the hidden mechanics the NHL’s best rely on, and shows you how to plug them into your game step by step.

If you’re ready to skate faster with less effort, flow through transitions, and move with the smoothness of the world’s best players, the Downhill Skating System is your blueprint to faster player development.

Aldrig sett så delade kommentarer som på Daunfeldt avsnittet Jag har aldrig på tio år sett en så bred spridning i kommentarerna 😂🙈

Avsnitt 475 med Svenskt Näringslivs chefsekonom Sven-Olov Daunfeldt om tillväxt, arbetstid och vad Sverige kan bli bättre på.

Kommentarerna gick från:

- "Jag blev lite äcklad i munnen. Är verkligen tillväxt det enda vi ska sträva efter?"
- Till "Det här är det bästa avsnittet, jag satt bara och nickade."
- Till de mer avvägda: vi ska vara stolta över den svenska modellen, där arbetsgivarorganisationer och fack tillsammans byggt det samhälle vi ville ha.

Jag har liten ambition att driva en agenda. Och jag tar till mig feedbacken: vi borde så klart också bjuda in LO:s chefsekonom och ställa samma frågor för att få ett annat perspektiv. Vilket vi kommer göra under hösten.

Vilka frågor tycker du att vi ska ta upp då? Skriv dem här nedanför.

videos.title: Claude 6: Anthropic’s $100B+ AI Bet to Beat GPT & Gemini?
videos.summary_source_text:
Claude 6: Anthropic’s $100B+ AI Bet to Beat GPT & Gemini? Link to our newsletter: https://bitbiased.ai/

There’s a $100 billion number being attached to Anthropic’s next-generation AI — but the real infrastructure picture may be closer to $200 billion. And there’s an even bigger problem with the hype: “Claude 6” does not officially exist.

Anthropic hasn’t announced Claude 6, published a release date, or revealed a parameter count. So instead of treating rumors like a product launch, this video separates what Anthropic has actually confirmed from what the internet has filled in — and asks whether its next major Claude model really has a shot at beating OpenAI’s GPT and Google Gemini.

The money is real. Anthropic announced a ten-year, $100 billion AWS compute commitment covering up to five gigawatts of capacity. But AWS is only part of the infrastructure story. Anthropic has also built major relationships with Microsoft Azure, Nvidia, Google Cloud, and AMD, including a two-gigawatt AMD GPU deal connected to a supercomputer called Helios.

Put the commitments and investments together, and the scale goes far beyond the $100 billion headline. But enormous compute spending doesn’t automatically produce the world’s best model. To understand whether the bet is working, we have to look at what Claude can actually do right now.

That’s where things get interesting.

Claude’s current models are posting serious numbers in coding and agentic workloads. Claude Opus 5 reportedly reached 96.0% on SWE-bench Verified, while Sonnet 5 scored 80.4% on Terminal-Bench 2.1. Opus 5 also posted 30.2% on ARC-AGI-3 versus a reported 7.8% for GPT-5.6, while reaching 64.7% on Humanity’s Last Exam according to the independent leaderboard cited in the video.

And the lineup just changed again. Anthropic released Claude Fable 5.1 and Mythos 5.1 on September 1, with Anthropic’s own numbers putting Fable 5.1 ahead of Opus 5 on several benchmarks, including roughly 81% on SWE-bench Pro. Those results are extremely new and self-reported, however, so they haven’t had the same independent scrutiny as older benchmark results.

Claude doesn’t win everywhere either. GPT still leads on broad academic knowledge in the MMLU comparison covered here, while another model edges Claude on BrowseComp. The emerging picture isn’t universal dominance — it’s specialization. Claude looks exceptionally strong at coding, agents, and sustained execution, while competitors retain advantages elsewhere.

The business numbers make that competition even more interesting. Ramp’s August payment data puts Anthropic at roughly 44% of surveyed enterprise AI spending versus OpenAI at 40%, while more than 1,000 companies are reportedly spending over $1 million per year on Claude.

But Anthropic’s trajectory has another complication: its fight with the Pentagon.

After refusing certain surveillance and lethal-use applications, Anthropic reportedly lost a roughly $200 million Department of Defense contract and was temporarily labeled a “supply chain risk,” before a federal court pushed back on that designation. It’s a revealing preview of the tension Anthropic could face as Claude becomes more autonomous and governments push for access to increasingly capable AI systems.

And autonomy appears to be exactly where Anthropic is heading. Its job postings describe models capable of writing, editing, testing, debugging, and shipping software end-to-end. Products such as Claude Cowork and Managed Agents point toward AI systems designed to keep executing tasks for hours with less human supervision.

That may be the real Claude 6 story.

The next leap might not be another chatbot with a higher benchmark score. It could be a model measured by how long it can reliably operate, build, debug, research, and execute before a human has to intervene.

So does “Claude 6” beat everyone? Not yet — because there is no officially announced Claude 6 to test. Anthropic has the compute, enterprise momentum, and increasingly powerful agentic models to make the possibility credible. But OpenAI still has major advantages, Google has the distribution power of Search and Android behind Gemini, and no amount of infrastructure spending guarantees a winner.

Until we get a released model and independent, side-by-side testing against the next GPT and Gemini, the biggest Claude 6 claims remain exactly that: claims.

04:35 Where Claude Actually Wins Right Now, and Where It Doesn't
07:41 The Fight Anthropic Picked With the Pentagon

11:25 The Verdict

Who Will Be the NHL's Next Big Trade? w/ Dave Pagnotta | Countdown To Hockey The NHL season hasn't even started yet, but the next wave of trade speculation is already beginning.

Daily Faceoff's Dave Pagnotta joins Countdown to Hockey to reveal the players and teams he's already watching as potential trade targets once the 2026-27 NHL season gets underway.

Pagnotta names Alex DeBrincat as the first player on his trade board, explaining why Detroit's uncertainty, Dylan Larkin's situation and DeBrincat's contract status could make him an intriguing name to watch as the season progresses.

He also identifies the Columbus Blue Jackets as a team worth monitoring if things don't go according to plan, with players like Adam Fantilli, Kirill Marchenko and other pieces potentially becoming part of the trade conversation.

But the biggest team to watch could be the New York Rangers. Pagnotta explains why New York's roster construction, potential regression and 13 pending free agents could give GM Chris Drury plenty of flexibility if the Rangers aren't where they want to be by the trade deadline.

Could the Rangers become major sellers? Which players could be moved? And when might the NHL's first significant trade of the season happen?

Dave Pagnotta breaks down the NHL's potential trade landscape before training camps even begin.

Stop Standing Up in Your Golf Swing If you tend to stand up through the ball, try thinking more like a hockey player.

Get into your posture, add a little pressure into the ground, and feel like you stay down through the shot instead of popping up out of it.

That slap shot feel can make it a lot easier to understand what staying in your posture should actually feel like.

And if you want some feedback while you practice it, the Blue Brick can give you a physical reference so you know when you’re keeping your hips back instead of moving toward the ball.

videos.title: Gemini 3.8 Flash Just Put Google Back On Top
videos.summary_source_text:
Gemini 3.8 Flash Just Put Google Back On Top Link to our newsletter: https://bitbiased.ai/

Google just shipped Gemini 3.8 Flash at $0.75 per million input tokens and $3.75 per million output tokens — while the more attention-grabbing Gemini 3.8 Flash Cyber remains locked behind a vetted access program.

That price difference could make the model anyone can actually use more consequential than the restricted one getting the headlines.

Google released two models under the Gemini 3.8 family on September 2. Standard Gemini 3.8 Flash is available to developers without a special application process, while Gemini 3.8 Flash Cyber — a specialized model designed for vulnerability discovery and patch generation — is restricted through Google's Fairwind Program.

But the biggest story may be the economics.

At $0.75 per million input tokens and $3.75 per million output tokens, Gemini 3.8 Flash dramatically undercuts the more expensive models discussed in this video. Claude Fable 5.1 is listed at $10 per million input tokens and $50 per million output tokens, while Claude Opus 5 comes in at $5 and $25 respectively.

A model doesn't necessarily need to dominate every benchmark to change how developers build products. If it's capable enough and cheap enough, suddenly high-volume AI workloads that were expensive to run become much easier to justify.

But that's where the benchmark story gets complicated.

Reported Gemini 3.8 Flash results on Terminal Bench 2.1 range from 81.6% to 90.8% depending on the source. That's a substantial spread for the same benchmark and model, raising questions about testing methodology, configurations, and exactly which number developers should trust.

On HLE Verified, Gemini 3.8 Flash reportedly scores 45.4. But the evidence available at launch still leaves an important verification problem: much of the strongest performance data comes from Google's own testing rather than a single reproducible independent evaluation.

That doesn't make Google's numbers wrong. It means developers should distinguish between a launch benchmark and independently validated performance before making production decisions.

There's another interesting part of this release: what Google chose to make openly available versus what it didn't.

Gemini 3.8 Flash is aggressively priced and broadly accessible. Gemini 3.8 Flash Cyber is gated behind the Fairwind Program for vetted government agencies, enterprise security teams, and partners. The distinction highlights the increasingly difficult line AI labs are drawing around dual-use cybersecurity capabilities: the same model that can help defenders discover vulnerabilities and generate patches could potentially help attackers find weaknesses first.

Then there are the details you won't get from a polished demo.

We still don't have enough independent evidence about Gemini 3.8 Flash's reliability across long-running agentic workflows, real-world production latency, or uptime at massive scale. And an aggressively low launch price doesn't guarantee that pricing remains unchanged indefinitely.

So who should actually test Gemini 3.8 Flash?

High-volume workloads are the obvious starting point: customer support automation, large-scale document summarization, structured data extraction, first-pass code review, and other applications where millions of API calls can turn small pricing differences into serious infrastructure costs.

For workloads where deep reasoning is the product, the decision is harder. The unresolved benchmark spread makes running Gemini 3.8 Flash against your own evaluation suite far more important than simply choosing whichever published score looks best.

For independent developers and smaller teams, though, the pricing alone makes Gemini 3.8 Flash difficult to ignore when evaluating a default model for a new project.

In this video, we break down exactly what Google shipped, how Gemini 3.8 Flash compares on price, what the benchmark numbers actually tell us, why Flash Cyber remains restricted, what Google's launch material doesn't answer, and whether this model deserves a place in your production stack.

The price gap is real. The verification gap is too.

CHAPTERS

00:00 Google Just Shipped Gemini 3.8 Flash

Google just shipped Gemini 3.8 Flash at $0.75 per million input tokens and $3.75 per million output tokens — while the more attention-grabbing Gemini 3.8 Flash Cyber remains locked behind a vetted access program.

That price difference could make the model anyone can actually use more consequential than the restricted one getting the headlines.

Google released two models under the Gemini 3.8 family on September 2. Standard Gemini 3.8 Flash is available to developers without a special application process, while Gemini 3.8 Flash Cyber — a specialized model designed for vulnerability discovery and patch generation — is restricted through Google's Fairwind Program.

But the biggest story may be the economics.

At $0.75 per million input tokens and $3.75 per million output tokens, Gemini 3.8 Flash dramatically undercuts the more expensive models discussed in this video. Claude Fable 5.1 is listed at $10 per million input tokens and $50 per million output tokens, while Claude Opus 5 comes in at $5 and $25 respectively.

A model doesn't necessarily need to dominate every benchmark to change how developers build products. If it's capable enough and cheap enough, suddenly high-volume AI workloads that were expensive to run become much easier to justify.

But that's where the benchmark story gets complicated.

Reported Gemini 3.8 Flash results on Terminal Bench 2.1 range from 81.6% to 90.8% depending on the source. That's a substantial spread for the same benchmark and model, raising questions about testing methodology, configurations, and exactly which number developers should trust.

On HLE Verified, Gemini 3.8 Flash reportedly scores 45.4. But the evidence available at launch still leaves an important verification problem: much of the strongest performance data comes from Google's own testing rather than a single reproducible independent evaluation.

That doesn't make Google's numbers wrong. It means developers should distinguish between a launch benchmark and independently validated performance before making production decisions.

There's another interesting part of this release: what Google chose to make openly available versus what it didn't.

Gemini 3.8 Flash is aggressively priced and broadly accessible. Gemini 3.8 Flash Cyber is gated behind the Fairwind Program for vetted government agencies, enterprise security teams, and partners. The distinction highlights the increasingly difficult line AI labs are drawing around dual-use cybersecurity capabilities: the same model that can help defenders discover vulnerabilities and generate patches could potentially help attackers find weaknesses first.

Then there are the details you won't get from a polished demo.

We still don't have enough independent evidence about Gemini 3.8 Flash's reliability across long-running agentic workflows, real-world production latency, or uptime at massive scale. And an aggressively low launch price doesn't guarantee that pricing remains unchanged indefinitely.

So who should actually test Gemini 3.8 Flash?

High-volume workloads are the obvious starting point: customer support automation, large-scale document summarization, structured data extraction, first-pass code review, and other applications where millions of API calls can turn small pricing differences into serious infrastructure costs.

For workloads where deep reasoning is the product, the decision is harder. The unresolved benchmark spread makes running Gemini 3.8 Flash against your own evaluation suite far more important than simply choosing whichever published score looks best.

For independent developers and smaller teams, though, the pricing alone makes Gemini 3.8 Flash difficult to ignore when evaluating a default model for a new project.

In this video, we break down exactly what Google shipped, how Gemini 3.8 Flash compares on price, what the benchmark numbers actually tell us, why Flash Cyber remains restricted, what Google's launch material doesn't answer, and whether this model deserves a place in your production stack.

The price gap is real. The verification gap is too.

Designed for both beginners and experienced traders, RIFT aims to simplify access to financial markets while providing users with tools that can help them participate more efficiently.

One of the key features of RIFT is its Auto Trading Engine, which allows users to allocate capital into automated trading strategies designed to operate without the need for constant monitoring. This enables participants to remain active in the markets without spending hours each day analyzing charts or placing trades manually.

For users who prefer direct market participation, RIFT also offers Manual Trading and Futures Trading functionality. This gives traders the flexibility to execute their own strategies, manage positions, and take advantage of market opportunities in real time.

RIFT is built around a non-custodial philosophy, meaning users maintain control of their own funds rather than depositing them into a centralized company account. This approach aligns with the growing demand for greater transparency, security, and user control within the digital asset industry.

Beyond trading, RIFT focuses heavily on education. Through training sessions, community support, and ongoing learning resources, users can develop a deeper understanding of trading, risk management, market psychology, and financial technology.

The platform also incorporates modern technologies such as AI-driven infrastructure, advanced execution systems, copy trading capabilities, and future integrations designed to create a more connected and intelligent trading environment.

PwC och OneMore Secure: Så stärker du cybersäkerheten i leverantörskedjan Cyberrisker i leverantörskedjan har blivit en strategisk fråga för många organisationer. Nya regulatoriska krav, ökade beroenden av externa leverantörer och ett mer komplext hotlandskap gör att företag behöver bättre insyn och kontroll över sina tredjepartsrisker. 

I denna korta film samtalar Henrik Petré, Partner Cyber Security på PwC Sverige, med Robert Willborg, Co-founder och Chief Security Officer på OneMore Secure, och Ulrika Fejne, cybersäkerhetsexpert och partneransvarig för samarbetet mellan PwC och OneMore Secure. 

Tillsammans diskuterar de: 

Varför leverantörskedjan är en växande cyberrisk 

Hur organisationer kan stärka sin digitala motståndskraft 

Vilka utmaningar och möjligheter som följer av NIS2 och andra regulatoriska krav 

Hur teknik, analys och rådgivning kan bidra till en mer effektiv hantering av tredjepartsrisker

This Tiny Squat Can Add Serious Speed 👀 If you’re just turning as fast as you can from the top, you’re probably leaving some power on the table.
Try this instead.

Get a little tighter into that trail glute, add a tiny squat, then shift and go.

That little load gives you something to actually push from instead of just spinning your hips.

Load. Squat. Shift. Go.

Your legs are strong. Use them!

The Ball First Board is great for practicing this because it gives you real feedback on the load and pressure shift so you can work on the sequence instead of guessing.

Want more speed? Don’t just spin from the top. Load the trail side, add a tiny squat, shift and GO. Your legs are strong. Use them. Comment “BALL FIRST” for the board. ⛳️

videos.summary_source_text:
How To Exploit Your Crossunders For Max Speed The Downhill Skating System is the mechanics-first approach that unlocks effortless, controlled speed on the ice without extra conditioning, pushing or “trying harder.” Inspired by the movement signatures of players like Connor McDavid, Nathan MacKinnon, Cale Makar, Quinn Hughes, and other elite NHL skaters, this system teaches you how to move on the ice with gravity, using your body's own stretch shortening cycles mixed with the most efficient footwork patterns and various skating mechanics.

Most players skate “uphill”: stiff, blocky, pushing hard, creating tension and burning energy like we were always taught in traditional powerskating. Downhill skating flips that model. By using counter rotation, proper joint angles, and natural gravitational momentum, we teach you move faster with less effort.

Inside the Downhill Skating System, players learn to:

1) Unlock the inner spring for better acceleration.
2)Use different footwork patterns to add options, deception and effortlessness. 
3)Proper joint alignment for efficiency and balance instead of creating tension with push strides.

Apply NHL-base mechanics like shin angle, Y-angle, rhythm and cadence. Generate speed using the rocker, with heel pressure and subtle weight transfers.

This system is not what players would learn in traditional, outdated power skating methods. It’s a biomechanics-based operating system designed to match your body type and natural movement patterns.

Whether you’re trying to improve the forward stride, lateral movements, deception, or posture, Downhill Skating reveals the hidden mechanics the NHL’s best rely on, and shows you how to plug them into your game step by step.

If you’re ready to skate faster with less effort, flow through transitions, and move with the smoothness of the world’s best players, the Downhill Skating System is your blueprint to faster player development.

From accepting your natural shot shape to choosing the right equipment and focusing on precise targets, these are simple concepts that can make a major difference in your scores.

You'll learn why tour players don't try to fix their swing during a round, how to play your natural fade or draw, and why proper driver fitting matters more than simply choosing a certain brand. We also explain why launch angle is so important for maximizing distance, how the release of the club affects launch conditions, and why hitting the driver higher can help you produce more distance with less spin.

videos.summary_source_text:
4 Things Speed Golf Taught Me About Playing Better Golf (US Speedgolf Open) I thought this was about trying to compete in a National Open. But what Speedgolf taught me about my actual golf game ended up being incredibly valuable.

This series is powered by Garmin. I wore the Fenix 8 for every run and every round of golf and highly recommend it: https://creatorlink.shop/4mW5ued

videos.title: Fable 5.1 Just Dropped: It’s 45% Cheaper & 2X Better
videos.summary_source_text:
Fable 5.1 Just Dropped: It’s 45% Cheaper & 2X Better https://bitbiased.ai/ai-automation-services
Anthropic says Fable 5.1 can be 45% cheaper while delivering more than double the performance of Fable 5 on some benchmarks. Both claims are technically real — but independent testing reveals a much stranger story.

Fable 5.1 arrived on September 1st, less than three months after Fable 5, and Anthropic is positioning the point upgrade as its new flagship for long, multi-step coding, scientific reasoning, research, and agentic workflows. The underlying specs haven't dramatically changed: the model keeps the one-million-token context window, 128,000-token output cap, and the same $10 per million input tokens and $50 per million output tokens.

What has changed is how the model uses those resources — and one setting can completely change whether Fable 5.1 looks like an incredible value or an expensive overkill machine.

The biggest performance gains are concentrated in long-horizon tasks. On Terminal-Bench-Science, Fable 5.1 scored 52.6%, compared with just 24.7% for Fable 5. AutomationBench jumped from 17.1% to 31.4%. But on shorter general-reasoning benchmarks, the difference is far less dramatic: Humanity's Last Exam moved from 57.8% to 60.9% without tools, while GDPval-AA reached 1,853 Elo versus Fable 5's 1,723.

Then there's the pricing story.

Anthropic cut prompt-cache read pricing by 75%, from $1 per thousand cached tokens to $0.25. For agentic workloads that repeatedly reuse large amounts of context, Anthropic says that can translate into roughly 25% lower typical costs and savings of up to 45%.

But independent testing from Artificial Analysis found something the headline pricing doesn't capture: at maximum effort, Fable 5.1 reportedly used roughly 1.7x as many output tokens as Fable 5 on the same composite task. That pushed the measured cost to $3.76 per task — around 20% more than Fable 5. Even at a reduced "extra-high" effort setting, the measured $2.72 cost remained above Opus 5's $2.34.

At low effort, however, the picture flips. Testing suggests Fable 5.1 can match Fable 5's quality for roughly one-quarter of the cost. The effort setting isn't just a minor optimization anymore — it can effectively turn Fable 5.1 into two very different products.

There's another unusual detail: Fable 5.1 and Mythos 5.1 reportedly use the exact same underlying weights. The difference is in their safety filters. Fable is broadly available to paid users, while Mythos is restricted to vetted organizations working in areas such as cybersecurity research and life sciences.

That distinction actually appears in benchmark results. Fable 5.1 scored 55.8% on Terminal-Bench 4.0, while Mythos 5.1 reached 60.9%. Anthropic's methodology indicates that safety refusals can count as zeroes on certain benchmarks, meaning some of the apparent performance difference comes from what each version is permitted to attempt rather than a difference in the underlying model.

Independent testing also gives Anthropic's broader performance claims some credibility. Artificial Analysis measured an Intelligence Index score of 66 for Fable 5.1 at maximum effort, ahead of Opus 5 at 63 and GPT-5.6 Sol at 61. But AA-Omniscience exposed another wrinkle: the model attempted more answers than Fable 5 while also making slightly more mistakes, producing essentially no improvement on that particular test.

And there is a privacy catch.

Anthropic's new Enterprise Frontier Safeguards can allow qualifying enterprise customers to keep conversation logs on their own cloud infrastructure under customer-controlled keys, with some large customers reportedly eligible for zero data retention. But for regular users, the default 30-day retention policy remains in place.

So who is Fable 5.1 actually for?

If you're running coding agents across large codebases, long research pipelines, scientific reasoning workloads, or tool-heavy tasks that repeatedly reuse context, the upgrade could be substantial. If you're mainly doing quick Q&A, light writing, or short prompts, the performance gains are much smaller — while Fable 5.1's pricing and latency can make Opus 5 or Sonnet 5 more sensible choices.

The real Fable 5.1 story isn't simply that Anthropic made a model that's "45% cheaper" or "twice as good." It's that the model's value changes dramatically depending on workload, cache reuse, and especially the effort level you select.

And that makes the effort slider arguably more important than the model name itself.

#anthropic #fable51 #ai #artificialintelligence #llm https://bitbiased.ai/ai-automation-services

videos.title: Swing away not towards you…
videos.channel: Better & Easier golf with your guide Marcus Edblad
videos.summary_source_text:
Swing away not towards you… Don’t make a fake swing path out by only changing your stance. Make it real and discover how an effortless swing should feel.

#golfswing #golf #golftips 

Online lesson are now a possibility on Skillest: https://skillest.com/app/profile/marcus-edblad

0:00 Intro to how to feel an effortless golf swing. 
1:00 Make it real not fake

Let me help you get an effortless golfswing with speed, distance and accuracy. I call it the circle of speed. A good release will help you to a better impact and longer drives and irons without slice and hook. How to swing a golf club need to be adjusted to your skill level and experience. 

Long and straight is the goal for everyone but it takes time. Try to focus on one thing not everything when you practise. Impact, face control and swingpath will always be the most important part to drill. We focus too much on rotation but no good golf shot will be executed just by rotating. 

We also need to understand that many myths in golf are misleading. Everything that you find on the internet isn’t true. Ben Hogan, Sam Snead are two of the legends that are often misunderstood.  To understand golf we need to take it step by step and learn every part of the swing before we move on to the next. It's like a big jigsaw puzzle that we all can figure out. 

I will never call a slice sexy but a high draw is beautiful in a very special way. Some pro's that hit draw: Rory McIroy, Xander Schauffele, Patrick Reed, Sepp Straka, Bryson Dechambeau  and many, many more. 

We shall not keep our head still, only start with the hips, look only at the ball or keep the left or right arm straight. Understand what do do with the club and let your body find the best way possible. 

This is not Rick Shiels, Saguto golf, Danny Maude, Meandmygolf, the Average Golfer, Malaska, Mark Crossfield, Alex Elliot Golf or Paige Spiranac. This is a method that anyone can learn if you give it a chance. 

If you use callaway, ping, titleist, takomo or taylor made clubs doesn’t matter you can learn to hit good golf shots. Your loft or your shaft on the club will not change but you can always get better. 

Find what inspires you. Golf basics are the same for everyone. The pga tour, longdrivers or other good golfers can all help you find better golf shots. Watch what they do instead of listed to what they say. Listen mostly to your body and figure out what you need to do to produce the same results as the pros on TV. Be careful when you watch a golf swing in slow motion. The result isn't always what the golfer is trying to do. Feel and real are seldom the same. 

We can find inspiration in a lot of things. You can find training motivation watching movies like Rocky, Tin Cup or Happy Gilmore and find mental inspiration in legends like Arnold Schwarzenegger, Hulk Hogan, Sylvester Stallone or Mike Tyson. Maybe we sometimes need to hear about crazy achievements from people like David Goggins, Jocko Willink, Ct Fletcher, Jim Rohn or Tony Robbins. 

Mike Malaska, Mike Austin, Mike Dunaway, Pete Cowen and Steve Pratt are some of my favorite golf instructors online. Find the tips that make your golf better. Decide what you want to hit. I teach a draw but many like a fade and nobody likes a hook or slice. 

Your hips or your lag is not the key to golf. Your hands will decide the shot and you can do like Tiger Woods and trust your hands. Teach your hands to hit different shots. Hit big hooks and slices to understand what happens. Only straight is not gonna teach you anything. 

Bryson Dechambeu and Kyle Birkshire can inspire you to hit it longer. Tiger Woods and Phil Mickelson can give you inspiration and motivation to test new things and new golf shots. Linn Grant, Viktor Hovland and Ludvig Aberg can show you the future of golf. 

The Masters, Players Championship, The Players, The Open and US Open can make you love golf even more. See the best in the world solve all the problems we all need to master any golf course. Golf is a craft and you need fantasy, feel and skills to master it.

Questions my videos will answer:

How to swing faster. How to hit longer. How to swing faster. How to hit your irons better. How to be better at anything. How to master the circle of speed. How to get a better short game. How to hit your wedge better. How to release the golf club. How to rotate in golf. Best tips for beginner golfers. How to hit down on the ball. How to hit up on the ball. How to rotate hips in the golf swing. How to hit straight every time. How to stop slicing. How to swing effortlessly. 

#subscribe #golftips #pga  #hurricane

videos.title: Svinga iväg från dig, inte mot dig…
videos.channel: Bättre & Enklare golf med Marcus Edblad PGA
videos.summary_source_text:
Svinga iväg från dig, inte mot dig… Skapa mer hastighet och kontroll med en sving som påminner mycket om ett enkelt kast.

Det är snart dags att tänka på vintergolf i simulator. Missa inte detta om du funderar på att köpa en ny simulator i år. Här kommer en presentation av GolfJoy som jag nu använt i ett år och är supernöjd med.

#golf #golftips #golfswing 

0:00 Intro till att svinga iväg inte emot dig

Nu finns det möjlighet att genom appen Skillest göra mig till din personliga tränare. Du hittar mig på denna länk: https://skillest.com/app/profile/marcus-edblad

Låt mig hjälpa dig finna bättre slag, bollträff, riktning och svinghastighet. Oavsett om du slår en wedge, järnklubba eller driver kan du med dina händer lära dig golfslag som du inte trodde var möjliga. Längre och rakare slag kräver alltid träning men något alla kan lära sig.

videos.title: You’re Prompting GPT-5.6 Sol Wrong: Here’s What Actually Works
videos.summary_source_text:
You’re Prompting GPT-5.6 Sol Wrong: Here’s What Actually Works Link to our newsletter: https://bitbiased.ai/

You’re probably prompting GPT-5.6 Sol completely wrong — and the problem may be that your prompts are too long, not too short.

OpenAI’s guidance for Sol pushes against a lot of conventional prompt-engineering advice: leaner, more specific prompts can work better than giant walls of roles, rules, repeated instructions, and elaborate reasoning frameworks. And according to the benchmarks discussed in this video, GPT-5.6 Sol at its lowest reasoning setting even outperformed GPT-5.5 at its highest.

So what does a good GPT-5.6 Sol prompt actually look like?

This video breaks the process down into a simple framework: Task, Context, Constraints, and Output — with Success Criteria added when the job needs a clearly defined finish line. Instead of relying on “magic words” or telling the model to act like an expert, the goal is to give Sol the same information a capable colleague would actually need before starting.

Then we put that framework through five very different real-world use cases: YouTube writing, research, coding, image generation, and data analysis.

For writing, we compare a vague request like “write a YouTube intro about AI agents” with a structured prompt that specifies the audience, length, tone, purpose, and desired result. The difference isn’t adding more words for the sake of it — it’s making every instruction carry useful information.

For research, the same framework becomes a way to control scope, sourcing, organization, and the distinction between facts and analysis. Rather than simply telling Sol to “research the AI coding assistant market,” the prompt defines exactly what should be investigated, which sources should be prioritized, and how the final research should be structured.

Coding introduces another problem: prompts that are either massively under-specified or overloaded with unnecessary personas. We test a landing-page request that specifies HTML, CSS, vanilla JavaScript, the required page sections, design direction, complexity limits, and output format — without needing a paragraph telling the model it’s a “senior frontend engineer.”

Image generation needs a slightly different kind of specificity. Subject matter alone isn’t enough. Composition, lighting, positioning, aspect ratio, mood, and negative constraints can determine whether an AI-generated YouTube thumbnail is immediately usable or needs another round of prompting. The example here explicitly places the robot on one side and reserves empty space for thumbnail text — a small instruction with a huge practical impact.

And with data analysis, the key shift is from asking Sol to describe your numbers to asking it to help make a decision. The test focuses on YouTube analytics including views, click-through rate, average view duration, and total watch time, then asks for five actionable insights rather than another summary of the spreadsheet.

But even a good framework can be undermined by bad habits.

Vague feedback like “make this better” still leaves the model guessing. Missing audience context changes the answer. Ignoring the desired output format hands important decisions back to the model. And treating the first response as the final response misses a major part of the workflow: prompt, review, refine, repeat.

The bigger lesson isn’t that prompting no longer matters. It’s that better models can change what good prompting looks like.

With GPT-5.6 Sol, the goal is not to write the longest instruction manual possible. It’s to identify the information that actually affects the result, state it clearly, define what success looks like when necessary, and then refine based on what the model gives you.

Task. Context. Constraints. Output. And, when needed, Success Criteria.

Try that structure on the next prompt you were already planning to send and see how much unnecessary instruction you can remove without giving up control.

videos.title: Are the Broncos Ready to Take the Next Step? | After the Horn
videos.summary_source_text:
Are the Broncos Ready to Take the Next Step? | After the Horn Tom Green and Woody Paige are back for another episode of After the Horn, breaking down the biggest stories across Colorado sports as football season gets underway.

Broncos Season Outlook

Denver brings back nearly its entire core, but is stability a strength or a sign of stagnation? Tom and Woody break down the Broncos’ roster, Jonathan Cooper’s uncertain status, Bo Nix, Davis Webb taking over play-calling duties and what Denver needs to survive a brutal opening stretch. They also look around the AFC West and debate whether the Broncos can challenge Kansas City this season.

NFL Stadiums

What should the Broncos prioritize if they build a new stadium? Woody and Tom discuss Arrowhead, Seattle, the old Mile High atmosphere and why an enclosed or domed stadium could make sense in Denver.

Colorado College Football

CU opens against Georgia Tech while Colorado State prepares for the Border War against Wyoming. The guys discuss Deion Sanders, Brennan Marion’s new offense, Jim Mora Jr.’s arrival at CSU and just how unpredictable college football has become in the transfer portal era.

Rockies Race to 100

The Rockies have lost a franchise-record 10 straight games at home and are once again closing in on 100 losses. Tom and Woody discuss Colorado’s young players, the direction of the organization and what matters most over the final month of the season.

Cale Makar & the Avalanche

Makar’s massive eight-year extension keeps one of hockey’s biggest stars in Colorado for the long haul. Does his commitment extend the Avalanche’s Stanley Cup window, and can this core add another championship?

Nuggets vs. Avalanche

Two teams under the same ownership appear to be heading in very different directions. Tom and Woody compare how the Avalanche and Nuggets are being managed, discuss Denver’s difficult salary-cap situation, Peyton Watson’s future and whether major changes could eventually be coming to the Nuggets.

Plus, Aaron Donald’s return to the NFL and a very important debate about airplane etiquette.

Watch the full episode of After the Horn with Tom Green and Woody Paige.

Over a billion people have sleep apnea, and the majority don’t know that simple airway exercises could offer a potential solution.

Sleep apnea involves a narrow airway with muscles that are too relaxed and weak. The airway can collapse, cutting off your oxygen and interfering with your sleep.

Most people with sleep apnea rely on a CPAP machine for sleep apnea treatment. People are also often told to lose weight to stop sleep apnea, but that only works in about a third of cases.

Do these sleep apnea exercises once a day for 7 minutes. Follow along for a simple demonstration of the following sleep apnea exercises:
1. Tongue root press — Hold pressure for 5 seconds, relax for 2 seconds, and repeat 15 times.
2. Palate lift — Hold the lift at the top for 3 seconds, release, and repeat for 20 reps.
3. Cheek suction and hold — Hold a fish face for 5 seconds, followed by a puff face. Complete 5 cycles.

videos.title: I Plugged a $20 ESP32 Into Claude Code: No Manuals
videos.summary_source_text:
I Plugged a $20 ESP32 Into Claude Code: No Manuals I plugged three cheap ESP32 boards into my Mac, one at a time, and had Claude Code work out what each one was and then write the firmware for it. No manuals, no Arduino tutorials, no libraries to wrestle with. 📌 WHAT I USED (all three boards: $63.96 total)...

Act I: Waveshare ESP32-C6 1.47" Display (~$20)
https://mrc.fm/esp32c6

Act II: ESP32 2.8" Touchscreen "Cheap Yellow Display" (~$18)
https://mrc.fm/esp32cyd

Act III: Waveshare ESP32-S3 1.54" e-Paper (~$26)
https://mrc.fm/esp32epaper

ALSO MENTIONED (not used in this build)
ESP32-S3 3-pack (~$19): https://mrc.fm/esp323pack
3.7V 3000mAh LiPo (~$10): https://mrc.fm/esp32lipo
JST 1.25mm pairs x30 (~$7): https://mrc.fm/esp32jst

Prices are US, August 2026, and they move. Outside the US your local Amazon usually carries the same boards, and buying direct from Waveshare is cheaper per board before shipping and import tax.

Some of the links above are affiliate links. If you buy through one I may earn a small commission at no extra cost to you.

Every board came out of the box as a black box. No model number, no documentation, nothing. Claude Code interrogated each one over the USB-C cable and told me what it was holding, right down to the Windows username of the person who built the factory firmware that was still sitting on it.

Then it built something different on each one, chosen because the board before it physically could not do the job.

Board one, the Waveshare ESP32-C6-LCD-1.47, $19.99 from Micro Center. It became a live window onto the Mediterranean off Paphos, with real sea temperature and wave height coming down the USB cable while the board's own radios stayed switched off. The factory firmware was 1.87 MB. What Claude Code wrote is 376 KB.

Board two, the 2.8 inch touchscreen everyone calls the Cheap Yellow Display, usually sold as the ESP32-2432S028R, $17.98. It became a Bluetooth audio spectrum analyser, so I can play a track on my phone and watch it move on the screen. This one was impossible on the first board, because the C6's Bluetooth does not carry audio at all. Claude Code spotted that difference on its own.

Board three, the Waveshare ESP32-S3-ePaper-1.54, $25.99. It became a camera for sound. It listens for five seconds and prints the room as artwork on e-paper, building the ink up over six passes like a Polaroid developing, and then it says something dry about what it just heard. Unplug it and the picture is still there.

There is a bug in here too, and it is the best bit. The first screen came up shifted and showing the old image underneath. I took a photo, pasted it straight into Claude Code, and it read the fault off the picture: shifted by 34 pixels, the classic signature of a row offset. That would have taken me a whole afternoon.

If you are a home labber or you tinker with Home Assistant, this is the video I wish existed when I started. I have been playing with these boards for over ten years and they have come a very long way from switching an LED on and off.

Nobody paid for this video and no board here was sent to me. I bought all of it with my own money at Micro Center in the United States and on Amazon. Waveshare do not know I exist.

Tell me in the comments which board you would buy and what you would make it do. Best idea gets built and featured in the next video, and there will be a next video.

Ferrari Purosangue v Lotus Eletre X v Lambo Huracán Perf: DRAG RACE Can the 2,615kg Lotus Eletre X really take down a Ferrari?! 

Explore new and used car deals with Carwow: https://bit.ly/Change-Your-Car-0209

Mat’s got his hands on the all-new Lotus Eletre X! 

It’s a hybrid version of Lotus’s high-performance SUV, and he’s going up against one of the most popular performance SUVs around - the Ferrari Purosangue! 

However, that’s not all. Whoever loses the initial race will then face a ‘proper’ performance car: a Lamborghini Huracan Performante! 

So let’s take a closer look at the stats…

The Ferrari is powered by a 6.5-litre naturally aspirated V12 that pumps out 725hp and 716Nm. Power is sent to all four wheels via an 8-speed auto gearbox, and it weighs in at 2,133kg. It’s easily the most expensive car here, with the starting price coming in at £364,000.

As for the Lotus, it’s equipped with a 2-litre turbocharged petrol engine and two electric motors. These combine to produce 952hp and 935Nm, with this power sent to all four wheels. It costs around £103,000, but it’s super heavy, tipping the scales at 2,615kg! 

Finally, we come to the Lambo. It’s powered by a 5.2-litre naturally aspirated V10 that delivers 640hp and 600Nm. It sends that power to all four wheels via a dual-clutch automatic gearbox, and it weighs in at just 1480kg. As of today, it’s worth around £215,000.

So does the 900hp Lotus have what it takes? There’s only one way to find out… LET’S RACE!
